"
},
# ... etc ...
}
Pydantic has built-in support for loading JSON, though sadly it doesn’t support reading from a file.
So we load the file into a string and then parse it:
with
open
(
"
customers.json
"
,
"
rb
"
)
as
f
:
raw_json
=

()

CustomerDirectory

)
This is very straightforward.
But there’s a problem.
If we
measure peak memory usage
, it’s using a
lot
of memory:
$
/usr/bin/time
-v
python v1.py
...
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 2071620
...
That’s around 2000MB of memory, 20× the size of the JSON file.
If our JSON file had been 10GB, memory usage would be 200GB, and we’d probably
run out of memory
.
Can we do better?
Reducing memory usage
There are two fundamental sources of peak memory usage when parsing JSON:
The memory used during parsing; many JSON parsers aren’t careful about memory usage, and use more than necessary.
The memory used by the final representation, the objects we’re creating.
We’ll try to reduce memory usage in each.
1. Memory-efficient JSON parsing
We’ll use
ijson
, an
incremental JSON parser that lets us
stream
the JSON document we’re parsing
.
Instead of loading the whole document into memory, we’ll load it one key/value pair at a time.
The result is that most of the memory usage will now come from the in-memory representation of the resulting objects, rather than parsing:

ijson
with

data
=
{}
# The empty string is part of ijson's query language,
# in this case it means "iterate over top-level", and
# since we're using kvitems() that means top-level
# key-value pairs in the root JSON object/dict:

cid
,
cust_dict
in
ijson
.
kvitems
(
f
,
""

# Create a Customer for the value dict:
customer
=
Customer

(

)
# Store it in the root dict using the key:
data
[
cid
]
=
customer
# And now create the root object:
directory
=
CustomerDirectory
.
model_validate
(
data
)
While parsing this way is significantly slower (5×), it reduces memory usage significantly, to just 1200MB.
It also requires us to do a bit more of the work of parsing the JSON, but anything below the top-level JSON object or list can be done by Pydantic.
2. Memory-efficient representation
We’re creating a lot of Python objects, and
one way to save memory on Python objects is to use “slots”
.
Essentially, slots are a more efficient in-memory representation for Python objects, where the list of possible attributes is fixed.
This saves memory at the cost of disallowing adding extra attributes to an object, which in practice isn’t that common so it’s often a good tradeoff.
Unfortunately,
pydantic.BaseModel
doesn’t seem to support that at the moment, so I switched to Pydantic’s dataclass support, which does.

文章主要讨论了如何在使用Pydantic模型加载大型JSON文件时减少内存消耗。默认情况下，Pydantic加载JSON文件会导致高内存使用，可能达到文件大小的20倍。为解决此问题，文章提出了两种主要方法：

1. **使用ijson库进行增量解析**：通过流式处理JSON文件，逐项加载数据，从而减少解析时的内存占用，但速度会变慢。
   
2. **使用带slots的数据类**：通过Pydantic的数据类支持和slots特性，固定对象属性以减少内存使用。

最终，结合这两种方法，可以将100MB JSON文件的峰值内存使用从2000MB减少到450MB。这些方法特别适用于需要处理大型JSON文件且内存资源有限的情况。

data.article_summary: Pi Labs推出了一款名为Pi Scorer的评分模型，具有高准确性和快速性，能够在不到100毫秒内评估20多个自定义维度，超越Deepseek和GPT 4.1。Pi Scorer适用于各种AI应用场景，包括离线评估、在线观察、训练数据质量和模型优化等，并可轻松集成到Google Spreadsheets等工具中。Pi Labs由Google前高管创立，将多年AI和搜索技术经验融入产品，帮助用户确定最佳评估指标并提供高效解决方案。
data.comments_summary:

补充讨论：

争议焦点：
• 产品演示的效果和UI设计是否合适是争议的主要焦点，eterm认为演示跳跃性强且UI过于复杂，而jmoore15则积极展示产品并寻求社区反馈。
• 品牌宣传的真实性和方式存在争议，bound008强调应诚实展示团队成就，而不是夸大其词。

总体来看，评论主要围绕产品演示的质量、品牌宣传的诚实性以及命名和品牌稀释问题展开讨论，同时也有个人背景和产品发布动机的分享。

data.title: Near-infrared spatiotemporal color vision enabled by upconversion contact lenses
data.author: ArnoVW
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类是否能够通过技术手段实现对红外线等不可见光的感知，以及这种技术的潜在应用和实际可行性。

不同观点：
• **interestica**：分享了自己配戴用于校准的隐形眼镜的经历，这种眼镜能够在极近的距离提供超高清的放大视觉效果，类似于显微镜的效果。他认为这种“视觉增强”技术可能对精细任务（如焊接）有帮助，并提出对现有技术下其他类型的视觉增强的兴趣。
• **mncharity**：质疑“人类无法感知红外线”的说法，指出人类实际上可以感知一定范围的近红外光（NIR），并引用了一些研究和DIY实验来支持自己的观点。
• **ArnoVW**：引用了科学研究，展示了通过佩戴近红外上转换隐形眼镜（UCLs）可以让人类识别近红外信息，甚至实现三原色近红外彩色视觉。该评论强调了这种技术在非侵入性红外视觉感知中的潜力。
• **m463**：通过提及红外感应卡的例子，说明了通过将红外光转换为可见光来实现感知的方式，类似于评论中提到的技术。
• **dvh**：提出了一种技术问题，询问是否可以通过非线性材料将红外光转换为可见光，并产生更高次谐波。
• **unsupp0rted**：对红外视觉技术的实际应用表示好奇，询问其可能的实用或有趣的用途。
• **amacbride**：以幽默的方式提到了《龙与地下城》中的“红外视觉”概念，暗示对这种技术的幻想和期望。
• **RicoElectrico**：指出这种技术需要额外的光学器件才能实用，并提到如果镜片无法正确聚焦，则其实用性会受到限制。
• **metalman**：对该技术的实际可行性持怀疑态度，认为其分辨率太低，无法用于实际场景，并提到相关研究指出该技术在闭眼时也能工作，但距离实际应用还有很长的路要走。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术问题包括红外光转换的原理、镜片聚焦问题以及分辨率的限制。
• 对红外视觉技术的潜在应用场景进行了探讨，包括娱乐、夜间观察和增强现实等。
• 争议的焦点在于这种技术目前的实用性和可行性，部分评论者对其前景持怀疑态度，而其他人则对其潜在的应用表示出兴趣和期待。

data.author: devgoth
data.article_summary: Whenish是一款内置于iMessage的应用程序，帮助用户快速、简便地计划活动。通过创建日期投票、分享空闲时间并实时获取回应，用户可以轻松找到最佳聚会时间，无需切换应用。其主要功能包括快速创建日期投票、选择多个空闲日期、实时响应以及直观的日历界面。使用方法简单，打开群聊、选择Whenish图标、挑选空闲日期并发送投票即可。适用于聚餐、旅行、家庭活动和工作会议等各种场合。用户评价高，隐私政策表明不收集任何数据。该应用免费，兼容iPhone和iPad，需iOS 17.6或更高版本。

44062919.article_summary: Whenish是一款内置于iMessage的应用程序，帮助用户快速、简便地计划活动。通过创建日期投票、分享空闲时间并实时获取回应，用户可以轻松找到最佳聚会时间，无需切换应用。其主要功能包括快速创建日期投票、选择多个空闲日期、实时响应以及直观的日历界面。使用方法简单，打开群聊、选择Whenish图标、挑选空闲日期并发送投票即可。适用于聚餐、旅行、家庭活动和工作会议等各种场合。用户评价高，隐私政策表明不收集任何数据。该应用免费，兼容iPhone和iPad，需iOS 17.6或更高版本。

data.title: What3Words – The Algorithm
data.author: Liftyee
data.article_summary: What3Words是一个通过三个词来分享位置的系统，全球被划分为3米见方的网格，每个网格有一个唯一的三词地址。该系统声称，单词的错误（如单复数变化或多加字符）会导致位置相距甚远，从而易于发现错误。然而，数据显示在城市中这种错误概率远高于其声称的“1 in 2.5 million”。该系统使用一种算法，将经纬度转换为三个词，算法包括将位置坐标转换为整数，并通过混淆步骤防止相邻位置的词相似。混淆过程还根据位置调整单词范围，以使用较简单词汇。该系统在紧急情况下可能导致问题，例如误导紧急服务。
data.comments_summary:

• [观点二 - dlryc2021] 对有人提出质疑表示赞赏，认为需要有人对信息进行验证，而不是轻易相信他人的说法。不过，dlryc2021并未明确表示支持文章撤下，只是对质疑精神表示支持。

补充讨论：
• sheo引用的OSM wiki页面具体提到了what3words公司曾有要求撤下相关内容的行为，表明其对专利保护的态度。
• 争议的焦点在于是否因为算法的专利保护就应该撤下相关文章，sheo认为应该撤下，而dlryc2021则关注于质疑信息本身的重要性。

44061225.article_content:
What3Words is a widely promoted system that is used for sharing a location using just three words. For example, ///
wedge.drill.mess
is located in Hyde Park.The globe is divided into 3m squares, each of which has a unique three word address to identify it.
They claim that mistakes – like
changing a word into a plural
, or
adding an extra character
– would result in a location so far away that you would detect the mistake. They have themselves
stated
“that people confuse plurals only about 5% of the time when hearing them read out loud”. This means the number of squares where this could be a problem is crucial. What3Words say the odds are “1 in 2.5 million” – but they seem to be under 1 in 100 in cities in the UK.
This might be OK if you are ordering takeaway, but if the application is directing emergency services to your location, these errors could cause serious problems.
If you just want the outcomes of this work, this
shorter blog post
might be a better read.
I’m going to describe the algorithm first and then go through the issues.
The Algorithm
What3Words can work entirely offline. A position is converted into words using an algorithm and a fixed word list of 40,000 words. This is described in their patent with enough level of detail that you can understand why it is fundamentally broken.
From a high level, the following steps are required:
A lat/lon is converted into a integer coordinate XYxy.
XYxy is converted into a single integer n representing position.
n is shuffled into m to prevent words in two adjacent squares being the same.
m is converted into i,j,k which index into the word list.
i,j,k are converted into words.
Convert Lat/Lon to XYxy
The first step is to convert the decimal lat/lon into an integer XYxy location. This is just another type of grid reference with nothing complex going on.
The globe is divided up into large cells described by XY.
The Y direction starts at 0 at latitude -90° (the South Pole) and increases to 4,320 at latitude +90° (the North Pole). The X direction start at 0 at longitude -180° and increases to 8,640 at longitude +180°. This gives a total of 37,324,800 cells.
X increases as we move right, Y increases as we move up.
If we look in central London, we can see the scale of these cells. They are 4638m high and around 2885m across in London.
Within each of these large cells are the individual location squares, described by xy. There are always 1546 in the y direction. The number in the x direction varies from 1545 at the equator down to 1 at the poles. This is because of the curve of the earth.
In our central London cell of X=4316 Y=3396, x can range between 0 and 962, and y between 0 and 1546, giving 1,487,252 positions in the cell.
We now have an integer coordinate to represent anywhere on the earth.
Convert XYxy to n
The next step is to convert XYxy into n. n is a single large number that describes each point on the earth.
First, the offset into the large XY cell is found, using a simple formula:
1546 * x + y
This means that we are just counting upwards in columns as we go across. The bottom left corner of a cell is shown below. If you move up in the y direction, add one. If you move across in the x direction, add 1546. For the green square below, x=3 y=3 results in an offset of 4641.
Of course, this offset is not a unique number on the globe. To make it unique, the starting point – q – is defined for each XY cell.
In our central London square of X=4316 Y=3396, q = 733306450. That means the bottom left corner, n = 733306450. We add the offset on as we move through the cell. The n value of the green square is therefore 733311091 (733306450 + 4641).
The overall formula is:
n = q + 1546 * x + y
Where does q come from? Well, it comes from a lookup table.
Why is this done? q is used to bias lower values of n into cities. Lower values of n are important in the next steps.
We now have a large integer n, describing each point on the earth.
Convert n to m
The n value increases entirely predictably as we move through a cell. This could lead to the words for each position only changing by one word as we move about.
To handle this, a shuffling step is added to convert n to m. This step is also used to reduce the range of words used in cities to shorter and less complex words so that the system is easier to use.
The n values are split into bands. The bands go 0 to 2500^3 -1, 2500^3 to 5000^3 -1 all the way up to 37500-40000^3 -1. 16 bands in total. I’m only going to be looking at the first band from now onwards.
The shuffing within each band is carried out using the following formula:
m = StartOfBand + (BigNumber * PositionInBand) mod SizeOfBand
The BigNumber changes for each band. For band 0, from 0 to 2500^3 – 1, we get the following formula:
m = (9401181443 * n) mod 2500^3
The modulus means that the range of m will never be greater than 2500^3. In combination with the next step, this means that only the first 2,500 words in the dictionary are going to be used in band 0 cells.

data.title: Does Earth have two high-tide bulges on opposite sides? (2014)
data.author: imurray
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：潮汐预测的复杂性及其历史和科学背景

不同观点：
• srean认为潮汐预测问题吸引了众多物理学和数学界的重量级人物，并提到开尔文爵士设计的潮汐预测机，以及乔治·达尔文等人的贡献。他将这种机器视为早期“机器学习”的例子，强调正弦函数作为通用逼近器的作用。
• jxjnskkzxxhx对牛顿是否会混淆力和位移表示怀疑，暗示对潮汐问题的传统解释可能存在误解。
• antonignini指出潮汐理论的数学复杂性，并提到潮汐在靠近天体时产生的重大影响，如潮汐破坏事件。
• HPsquared描述潮汐为受月球移动激发的复杂水运动，强调其非简单的全球波动性质。
• MostlyStable提到在研究生课程中未深入学习潮汐问题，并对传统潮汐隆起的解释表示疑惑。
• mkl分享了一个有关潮汐动画的资源链接，提供了进一步了解潮汐动态的工具。
• tylervigen对教育中使用潮汐隆起图示表示质疑，认为其可能导致误解，建议使用更准确的简化模型。
• CommenterPerson基于个人观察提出简化假设，建议将地球视为光滑刚性球体，并探讨潮汐的12小时周期性。
• alejohausner关注动画中新西兰周围的潮汐追逐模式。
• chermi总结牛顿在潮汐力上的解释是正确的，但未涵盖全部故事，强调海洋深度和边界条件的影响。
• why_at表达了对潮汐问题复杂性的顿悟。
• coolcase建议从时空曲率的角度理解潮汐问题。
• imurray分享了自己在面试中对潮汐问题回答失误的经历，反映对该问题理解的不足。
• joshmarinacci认为牛顿的解释不完整而非错误。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及潮汐预测的历史机器和科学家的贡献，特别是开尔文和乔治·达尔文的贡献。
• 对传统潮汐隆起图示在教育中的有效性存在争议，部分评论者认为其会导致误解。
• 强调了潮汐问题的复杂性和数学难度，尤其是在涉及实际海洋和地球结构时。
• 个人观察和假设提供了对潮汐现象的简化理解，但同时也指出了这些模型的局限性。

争议焦点：
• 传统潮汐隆起图示在教育中的使用是否适当。
• 牛顿对潮汐力的解释是否不完整或易被误解。

data.title: How to cheat at settlers by loading the dice (2017)
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种在《卡坦岛》游戏中通过作弊骰子获得优势的方法，并用p值证明这种作弊难以被发现。作者通过将骰子浸泡在水中的简单方法制造了偏向骰子，使其更频繁地掷出6。经过4310次掷骰实验，数据显示6的出现概率显著高于其他数字。利用这种偏向骰子，玩家可以在游戏中平均每局获得5-15张额外的资源卡。文章还讨论了科学检测方法在实际游戏中无法有效证明骰子被动了手脚，因为偏差的微小程度使得标准科学测试不足以在游戏环境下检测出不公平。最后，文章通过计算展示了作弊玩家如何通过策略性放置定居点来最大化利用 biased 骰子的优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：骰子的公平性、作弊检测以及对游戏体验的影响

不同观点：
• [yellowapple] 认为普通骰子由于挖去点数的质量差异会导致偏差，特别是在便宜的游戏骰子中。这种偏差在一些游戏规则中被考虑，如Farkle中1比6更有价值。
• [n2d4] 提出使用暗动手脚但无人知晓具体偏向的骰子可以增加游戏策略性，但也指出当玩家开始计算时，这种策略性会减弱。
• [rtpg] 讨论了《卡坦岛》流行后，公开交易和骰子决定结果的机制在现代游戏设计中逐渐消失，尤其是公开交易不再受欢迎。
• [bee_rider] 认为在《Risk》或《Monopoly》中使用作弊骰子可能更有意义，而在《卡坦岛》中，策略更依赖于交易和时机。
• [misja111] 提供了一个简单的检测作弊骰子的方法：将骰子放入水中观察是否每次都同一面上浮。

补充讨论：
• [vunderba] 提到赌场使用半透明骰子是为了更容易检查是否被加权。
• [hinkley] 分享了一次由于疑似 biased 骰子而导致游戏结果偏向的经历。
• [asciimov] 基于自己的经验指出《卡坦岛》中的木制骰子存在偏差，并建议通过混合不同材质和大小的骰子来减轻这种影响，同时批评了骰子卡牌使游戏变得机械化。

how to cheat at settlers by loading the dice
(and prove it with p-values)
posted on 2017-12-14
tl;dr
This post shows how to create loaded dice, and how to use these dice to gain between 5-15 additional resource cards per game of Settlers of Catan.
Surprisingly, weâll prove that standard scientific tests are not powerful enough to determine that the dice are unfair while playing a game. This essentially means that itâs impossible for your opponents to scientifically prove that youâre cheating. This impossibility is due to methodological defects in the current state of scientific practice, and weâll highlight some ongoing work to fix these defects.
Loading the dice
My copy of Settlers of Catan came with two normal wooden dice. To load these dice, I placed them in a small plate of water overnight, leaving the 6 side exposed.
The submerged area absorbed water, becoming heavier. My hope was that when rolled, the heavier wet sides would be more likely to land face down, and the lighter dry side would be more likely to land face up. So by leaving the 6 exposed, I was hoping to create dice that roll 6âs more often.
This effect is called the
bias
of the dice. To measure this bias, my wife and I spent the next 7 days rolling dice while eating dinner. (She must love me a
lot
!)
In total, we rolled the dice 4310 times. The raw results are shown below.

Looking at the data, itâs âobviousâ that our dice are biased: The 6 gets rolled more times than any of the other numbers. Before we prove this bias formally, however, letâs design a strategy to exploit this bias while playing Settlers of Catan.
A strategy for loaded dice
The
key to winning at Settlers of Catan
is to get a lot of resources. We want to figure out how many extra resources we can get using our biased dice.
First, letâs quickly review the rules. Each settlement is placed on the corner of three tiles, and each tile has a number token. Whenever the dice are rolled, if they add up to one of the numbers on the tokens, you collect the corresponding resource card. For example:
A good settlement will be placed next to numbers that will be rolled often.
To make strategizing easier, the game designers put helpful dots on each token below the number. These dots count the ways to roll that tokenâs number using two dice.
We can use these dots to calculate the probability of rolling each number. For example, a
\(4\)
can be rolled in three ways. If we name our two dice
\(A\)
and
\(B\)
, then the possible combinations are
\((A=1,B=3)\)
,
\((A=2,B=2)\)
,
\((A=3,B=1)\)
. To calculate the probability of rolling a 4, we calculate the probability of each of these rolls and add them together. For fair dice, the probability of every roll is the same
\((1/6)\)
, so the calculation is:
\[\begin{align}
Pr(A+B = 4)
&= Pr(A = 1)Pr(B=3) + Pr(A=2)Pr(B=2) + Pr(A=3)Pr(B=1)    \\
&= (1/6)(1/6) + (1/6)(1/6) + (1/6)(1/6)              \\
&= 1/12                                 \\
&\approx 0.08333
\end{align}\]
For our biased dice, the probability of each roll is different. Using the numbers from the table above, we get:
\[\begin{align}
Pr(A+B = 4)
&= Pr(A = 1)Pr(B=3) + Pr(A=2)Pr(B=2) + Pr(A=3)Pr(B=1)    \\
&= (0.151)(0.157) + (0.169)(0.169) + (0.157)(0.151)      \\
&= 0.07597
\end{align}\]
So rolling a
\(4\)
is now less likely with our biased dice. Performing this calculation for each possible number gives us the following chart.
All the numbers below
\(7\)
are now less likely, and the numbers above 7 are now more likely. The shift is small, but it has important strategic implications.
Consider the two initial settlement placements below.
The
naughty
player knows that the dice are biased and puts her settlements on locations with high numbers, but the
nice
player doesnât know the dice are biased and puts her settlements on locations with low numbers. Notice that if the dice were fair, both settlement locations would be equally good because they have the same number of dots.
The following formula calculates the average number of cards a player receives on each dice roll:
\[
\text{expected cards per roll} = \sum_{\text{adjacent tokens}} Pr(A+B=\text{token value})
\]

data.title: When good pseudorandom numbers go bad
data.author: chewxy
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在实际计算机环境中计算矩阵特征分解时可能出现的误差，引用了Wilkinson（1965）的分析，指出由于浮点运算的特性，计算结果可能与理论值有出入，甚至在处理非对称矩阵时，实际计算的特征值可能与理论上的实特征值不一致。文章还描述了作者的同事在使用R语言进行多变量正态分布模拟时遇到的再现性问题，尽管使用了`set.seed()`来控制随机数生成器状态，但在不同机器上仍得到不同的结果。经过调查，发现问题并非出在`set.seed()`或`MASS::mvrnorm()`函数本身，而是由于浮点运算的固有误差导致的。这提醒我们，计算机运算并不总是符合预期，浮点运算的特性可能引发不易察觉的错误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机科学中随机函数与哈希函数的区别及其在不同情境下的使用问题，特别是关于结果的可 reproducibility（可重现性）的讨论。

不同观点：
• [somat] 认为随机函数和哈希函数有本质区别。哈希函数是确定性的，而随机函数则不是，且不应期望随机函数在不同版本或系统间有一致的结果。随机函数被误用作哈希函数是常见问题，导致对可重现性的误解。

• [AlotOfReading] 指出，多数人其实关注的是结果的可重现性，而非数值稳定性或准确性。现代硬件在遵循一些基本原则（如同样的输入、同样的操作顺序等）的情况下，可以实现可重现性。然而，由于工具链的实现问题和用户认知不足，这一特性未被优先考虑。

• [jam0wal] 提出，如果需要恒定的输出，直接使用常量数组比误用随机函数更合适，避免将个人偏见强加在对随机函数的错误理解上。

• [coolcase] 对问题本质感到困惑，询问是否与硬件差异、浮点运算的随机性或竞争条件有关，暗示对随机性和可重现性的技术背景缺乏了解。

补充讨论：
• [mjcohen] 分享了个人经验，提到过去在Fortran编程中遇到的性能问题，如数组下标检查对运行时间的影响，但未直接参与随机函数和哈希函数的讨论。

争议焦点：
• 随机函数和哈希函数的误用是争议的核心，特别是对随机函数的可重现性期望过高，导致实际应用中的困惑。
• 对现代硬件和工具链能否实现可重现性存在不同看法，一部分人认为在特定条件下是可行的，而另一部分人则认为工具链支持不足导致实际应用中的困难。

Computing the eigendecomposition of a matrix is subject to errors on a real-world computer: the definitive analysis is Wilkinson (1965). All you can hope for is a solution to a problem suitably close to x. So even though a real asymmetric x may have an algebraic solution with repeated real eigenvalues, the computed solution may be of a similar matrix with complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues.
–
help("eigen")
A few weeks ago, in the beforetimes when I’d not personally had the soul-crushingly unpleasant experience of being infected with that covid-19 thing,
1
some colleagues
2
approached me to talk about a reproducibility issue they’d been having with some R code. They’d been running simulations that rely on generating samples from a multivariate normal distribution, and despite doing the prudent thing and using
set.seed()
to control the state of the random number generator (RNG), the results were not computationally reproducible. The same code, executed on different machines, would produce different random numbers. The numbers weren’t “just a little bit different” in the way that we’ve all wearily learned to expect when you try to force computers to do mathematics. They wer painfully, brutally, catastrophically, irreproducible different. Somewhere, somehow, something broke.
3
4
That’s not supposed to happen…
Somehow, “Palpatine” returned. Palpatine was floating point errors all along.
… and to be fair, in most situations it
doesn’t
happen. Most computations are reproducible, and even random number generation does what it’s supposed to do as long as you’re careful with the seed. Or, to put it more plainly, the
set.seed()
method for controlling the results of your computations in R works just fine. At the risk of being tiresome, here’s a “random” permutation of the letters of the English alphabet that we obtain in R after the seed is fixed:
set.seed
(
1
L)
sample
(letters)
[1] "y" "d" "g" "a" "b" "k" "n" "r" "w" "j" "f" "t" "q" "x" "i" "e" "u" "l"
[19] "s" "p" "o" "m" "v" "z" "c" "h"
Here is
THE SAME BLOODY PERMUTATION
of those letters, produced a second time because the author is bored and she wants you to understand that this is a quarto document so everything that you see here is being done in an actual R session and she is not making it up:
set.seed
(
1
L)
sample
(letters)
[1] "y" "d" "g" "a" "b" "k" "n" "r" "w" "j" "f" "t" "q" "x" "i" "e" "u" "l"
[19] "s" "p" "o" "m" "v" "z" "c" "h"
Because the original code and the replication code both use
set.seed(1)
before calling
sample()
to shuffle the letters of the alphabet into a random order, we get the
same
random permutation in both cases. And although I’m executing this code twice on the same machine, there’s no reason to expect that it would make a difference if I ran the original code on my ubuntu laptop running R 4.4.3 or on a window machine running R 4.3.1. It “should” be the same result either way. I mean… that’s the whole purpose of
set.seed()
. It’s “supposed” to make your code reproducible, even though you are doing “random” things with that code. Right?
Well. It might. If you’re lucky.
That’s not what my colleagues experienced with their code when generating multivariate random normal samples. In their case, different machines produced different random samples even though the code used
set.seed()
to (ostensibly) prevent that from happening. Quite reasonably, their first thought was “
WHAT THE FUCK IS THIS???
”.
Having encountered the problem, their second thought was that it was their fault:
they
must have done something wrong with their code that caused the simulations to break. It wasn’t that. Their code was fine. Their third thought was that something was wrong with R itself, or more precisely with
MASS::mvrnorm()
, since this is the function that was causing all the difficulty. They couldn’t see anything wrong with the function though, so they asked me to look into it.
My first thought, when they oh-so-innocently dropped a nuclear weapon on my desk, was that MASS could not possibly be the problem. I mean, not really. It’s a very carefully tested package, it is very widely used, it’s fine. Right? Though… actually, now that I think of it
MASS::mvrnorm()
is a very old function, and it makes some assumptions about what happens at a lower level that might not be right. So… maybe it is the problem??? I don’t really know…
Look, it’s complicated okay?
So let me get back to you on that because when you track down far enough, the root cause of the problem my colleagues ran into wasn’t really the MASS package. The actual problem turned out to be the inconvenient fact that
floating point arithmetic
does not behave like real arithmetic, and that in turn has the teeeeensy tiny side effect that computers very often don’t do what people expect them to do.
Le sigh.
I should have known. In hindsight it was so obviously going to be floating point issues
5
that I shouldn’t have spent hours/days/weeks looking into it. As I said on Mastodon at the time:
In future, w

data.title: Practicing graphical debugging using visualizations of the Hilbert curve
data.author: akkartik
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用Lua和LÖVE框架通过图形化调试来理解Hilbert曲线的计算过程。Hilbert曲线的计算函数较为复杂，作者通过递归和图形可视化逐步解析其逻辑。最初，作者对函数中的交换、旋转以及负号感到困惑，于是通过多次迭代和图形化工具进行调试。作者首先直接绘制曲线，随后打印函数调用过程以更好理解递归步骤，尤其是当递归深度较小时，输出更加可控和直观。最终，这种图形化调试方法帮助作者深入理解了Hilbert曲线的生成原理。

不同观点：
• [fidotron]认为可以使用Logo/Turtle图形来处理递归分形。这种方法依赖于角度保持不变，并根据尺度做出局部决定，以避免过于关注细节，从而解决类似于海岸线悖论的问题。

补充讨论：
• [fidotron]提到了一个具体的技术——Logo/Turtle图形，这种技术在处理递归分形时能够有效管理角度和尺度问题。
• 引用的海岸线悖论（Coastline Paradox）是一个重要的概念，它解释了在测量复杂几何形状时遇到的困难，进一步支持了使用局部决策方法来处理分形的观点。
• 该评论暗示了递归分形中可能出现的测量问题，并提出了通过忽略过小细节来简化问题的解决方案。

“

For a while now
I've been advocating for a particular style of programming:
Use tools that don't change too often.
Use tools that don't keep historical accidents around indefinitely.
Minimize moving parts. Avoid additional third-party libraries, and forswear native libraries entirely.
Lua and
LÖVE
have been one nice way to get these properties. As I've used them, I've enjoyed an additional benefit: the ubiquitous presence of a canvas I can draw on as I program. This has been new to me with my erstwhile conservative and terminal-bound habits, and I've been pushing myself to lean more on graphics to understand what my programs are doing. Here I want to share one such experience. I'm using my run-anywhere
Lua Carousel
app, and you can paste the programs directly into it, but the workflow translates to any platform with a canvas.
A few weeks ago
Jack Rusher
shared a baffling function to compute the
Hilbert curve
. Here it is, translated to Lua:
function
h(x, y, xi, yi, xj, yj, n)
if
n <= 0
then
return
{x+xi/2+xj/2, y+yi/2+yj/2}
end
return
array_join(
h(x, y, xj/2, yj/2, xi/2, yi/2, n-1),
h(x+xi/2, y+yi/2, xi/2, yi/2, xj/2, yj/2, n-1),
h(x+xi/2+xj/2, y+yi/2+yj/2, xi/2, yi/2, xj/2, yj/2, n-1),
h(x+xi/2+xj, y+yi/2+yj,  -xj/2, -yj/2, -xi/2, -yi/2, n-1))
end
When I first looked at it, I could see a few superficial facts:
It returns an array of points containing
x
and
y
coordinates.
It's recursive. There's a base case for “leaf” calls, and each non-base case makes 4 recursive calls.
Only the base case actually “draws” by adding points to the result.
Non-leaf calls recursively partition the given square into 4 quadrants. Square size (the
xi
/
yi
/
xj
/
yj
) is being halved each time.
But the details were still unclear. Why the swaps/rotations? Why the negative signs in one of the 4 quadrants? Looking for answers led me to several iterations and some graphical infrastructure that promises to help with my next debugging task.

The first thing to look at is the curve itself.

pts = h(60, 60, 800, 0, 0, 800, 5)

the L-system based implementation on Wikipedia

44065146.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用Lua和LÖVE框架通过图形化调试来理解Hilbert曲线的计算过程。Hilbert曲线的计算函数较为复杂，作者通过递归和图形可视化逐步解析其逻辑。最初，作者对函数中的交换、旋转以及负号感到困惑，于是通过多次迭代和图形化工具进行调试。作者首先直接绘制曲线，随后打印函数调用过程以更好理解递归步骤，尤其是当递归深度较小时，输出更加可控和直观。最终，这种图形化调试方法帮助作者深入理解了Hilbert曲线的生成原理。

data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 牛津大学考古学家Juan de Lara教授领导的一项为期四年的多学科研究揭示了古希腊帕特农神庙的照明秘密。通过结合考古证据与3D技术和光学物理，研究重建了神庙的照明系统，显示出其设计旨在营造敬畏和虔诚的氛围。研究表明，帕特农神庙的建筑师和雕塑家菲迪亚斯 strategically 利用了屋顶开口、内部水池、窗户布局以及抛光大理石的反射特性来控制自然光和人工光。特别的是，在泛雅典娜节期间，日出光线会精确地通过东门照亮雅典娜雕像的金色长袍，产生耀眼的效果。该研究强调了技术在考古研究中的重要性，并正在被开发为虚拟现实体验以供公众体验。

44030263.article_content:
A four-year multidisciplinary study led by Oxford University Archaeologist Professor Juan de Lara has shed new light on a millennia-old mystery: how the
iconic Parthenon temple
on the Acropolis was illuminated in ancient Greece. By ingeniously combining archaeological evidence with cutting-edge 3D technology and optical physics, Professor de Lara has meticulously recreated the temple’s lighting system, revealing how it was designed to create a sense of awe and reverence.
The research, supported by UCL and The London Arts and Humanities Partnership (LAHP), and published today in the prestigious journal The Annual of the British School at Athens, demonstrates that the
Parthenon’s architects
and the renowned sculptor Phidias strategically incorporated various elements to manipulate both natural and artificial light. These features included carefully positioned roof openings, interior water basins, strategically placed windows, and the reflective properties of the finely polished marble.
Professor de Lara’s detailed 3D model even incorporated the colossal ivory and gold statue of Athena, created in 438 BCE, assigning precise material properties to its surfaces to analyze light reflection. By calculating the sun’s position during different times of the day and year in the 5th century BCE as light entered the east-facing doorway, the study revealed fascinating insights.
Enriched frontal view of the interior of the Parthenon. Credit: Juan de Lara
The findings suggest that the interior of the
Parthenon
was generally kept dim, fostering an atmosphere of reverence. However, during the weeks surrounding the Panathenaic Festival, a significant procession honoring the goddess Athena held every four summers, a remarkable phenomenon would have occurred. For several mornings, the rising sun would have aligned perfectly with the temple’s entrance, casting a brilliant beam of light directly onto the golden robes of Athena’s statue, creating a breathtaking, shimmering spectacle.
“Imagine entering the Parthenon—your eyes, still weary from the bright sun outside, slowly adjusting to the gradual darkness within,” describes Professor de Lara. “As sunlight filters through the temple’s doorway, it strikes the gold of the goddesses’ robes with a luminous vertical beam. This was the effect the architects and Phidias intended to create. It must have been magical!”
Professor de Lara emphasizes the importance of technology in archaeological research, stating, “To unlock the full potential of archaeological discoveries, we must keep embracing technology and digital tools as essential partners in exploration and research.”
The Parthenon, constructed between 447 and 432 BCE, is widely regarded as a pinnacle of classical architecture. While previous scholars, such as the French architect Antoine-Chrysostome Quatremère de Quincy and later James Fergusson, had pondered the temple’s lighting, Professor de Lara’s work provides concrete evidence of the sophisticated design and the crucial role light played in the visual and spiritual experience within.
To further enhance public understanding and engagement, Professor de Lara is currently transforming his research into an immersive virtual reality (VR) experience. This will be offered free to museums and educational centers, allowing visitors to virtually step inside the ancient Parthenon and witness the awe-inspiring effect of light on the colossal statue of Athena firsthand.
This remarkable research, bringing together archaeology and cutting-edge technology, makes the wonders of the ancient world accessible to everyone. For a truly immersive understanding of how light shaped the visual and spiritual experience within the Parthenon, explore the full 3D reconstruction available at
https://parthenon3d.com/.

data.title: Trade Secrecy in Willy Wonka's Chocolate Factory (2009)
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了罗尔德·达尔的小说《查理和巧克力工厂》中涉及的商业秘密法律问题。作者Jeanne C. Fromer指出，虽然小说主要是一部奇幻作品，但其情节实际上反映了现实糖果行业中广泛存在的商业秘密保护现象。文章讨论了在商业领域中对秘密信息保护的需求，以及商业秘密与专利法之间的关系，提出了对商业秘密法律保护的根本性疑问。通过分析如Hershey和Mars等实际企业，文章揭示了商业秘密在糖果行业中的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《查理和巧克力工厂》中旺卡的行为及其商业秘密保护的合理性分析

不同观点：
• **FridayoLeary的观点**：认为旺卡在竞赛胜利者资格和商业秘密保护方面缺乏限制是不合理的。他指出旺卡对孩子的残酷行为以及自恋的性格，认为他有能力并会采取严厉措施对付泄露秘密的胜利者，以此保护他的商业机密。这种做法被视为旺卡成功的原因之一。

• **alwa的观点**：对故事中旺卡及其竞争对手的行为感到困惑。他指出旺卡的竞争对手没有试图通过购买大量巧克力棒来赢得金券以刺探工厂的秘密是不合理的。同时，alwa提到Slugworth可能从过去的经验中学到教训，选择了招募人员而非安插间谍，这显示了一种竞争中的精明策略。

补充讨论：
• **staplung的观点**：提到《Futurama》中的Slurm工厂，通过链接提供了一个与讨论相关的幽默对比，但没有深入分析。

• **MarkusQ的观点**：提到《The Candymakers》一书，可能意在指出类似题材在其他作品中的处理方式，但没有详细阐述。

争议焦点：
• 旺卡在故事中对商业秘密的保护是否合理，尤其是他没有明确限制胜利者资格和信息使用。
• 竞争对手为何没有采取更积极的行动来获取旺卡工厂的秘密，这种行为是否符合商业逻辑。

整体来看，讨论主要围绕旺卡的行为合理性及其在商业竞争中的策略展开，部分评论者对其行为动机和商业逻辑提出了质疑和不同解读。

Abstract
Roald Dahl’s "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory" is well-known as a dark fantasy in which five children win a visit to a whimsical candy company.  Less conspicuous is the legal issue of trade secrecy driving the novel’s plot.  Secrecy is not indigenous to fictional representations of the candy industry, but is widespread throughout its real-world confectionary counterparts of today and yesteryear.  An investigation of the need for secrecy in this commercial sphere raises fundamental questions about the role of legal protection for misappropriations of secrets when actual secrecy seems to be paramount and about the relationship between trade secrecy and patent law.

不同观点：

• **alwa的观点**：对故事中旺卡及其竞争对手的行为感到困惑。他指出旺卡的竞争对手没有试图通过购买大量巧克力棒来赢得金券以刺探工厂的秘密是不合理的。同时，alwa提到Slugworth可能从过去的经验中学到教训，选择了招募人员而非安插间谍，这显示了一种竞争中的精明策略。

data.title: Problems in AI alignment: A scale model
data.author: hamburga
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了AI对齐（AI Alignment）问题，指出其核心是引导AI系统符合个人或群体的目标、偏好或伦理原则。作者将其比作一个 meme，认为其他领域如医药或教育同样需要对齐，但没有类似的专门概念。作者解释，这是因为AI对齐带有技术性，而其他领域的对齐更多涉及社会、伦理和市场等外部因素。文章强调，AI对齐不仅是个技术问题，还包括如何通过选择、讨论、规制等方式引导AI影响社会，这涉及更广泛的社会参与和复杂的系统运作。最终，作者提出，忽视这一点是错误的，并提供了一个链接，介绍了一种提高选择效率的社会技术协议。

主要讨论点：AI对齐（AI Alignment）问题的本质及其重要性

不同观点：

• **verisimi**：认为人类通过集体意志可以选择和引导AI的使用，但同时也存在被公司或权力中心操控的风险。

• **daveguy**：认为如何使用和与AI互动是个体和集体的选择问题，人类仍然可以选择不赋予AI控制权。

44065775.article_content:
After trying too hard for too to make sense about what bothers me with the AI alignment conversation, I have settled, in true Millenial fashion, on a meme:
Explanation:
The
Wikipedia article on AI Alignment
defines it as follows:
In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), alignment aims to steer AI systems toward a person’s or group’s intended goals, preferences, or ethical principles.
One could observe: we would also like to steer the development of
other things
, like automobile transportation, or social media, or pharmaceuticals, or school curricula, “toward a person or group’s intended goals, preferences, or ethical principles.”
Why isn’t there a “pharmaceutical alignment” or a “school curriculum alignment” Wikipedia page?
I think that the answer is “AI Alignment” has an implicit technical bent to it. If you go on the
AI Alignment Forum
, for example, you’ll find more math than Confucius or Foucault.
On the other hand, nobody would view “pharmaceutical alignment” (if it were formulated as “[steering] pharmaceutical systems toward a person’s or group’s intended goals, preferences, or ethical principles”) as primarily a problem for math or science.
While there always are things that pharmaceutical developers can do
inside the lab
to at least try to promote ethical principles  – for example, perhaps, to minimize preventable hazards, even when not forced to – we also accept that ethical work is done in large part
outside
of the lab; in purchasing decisions, in the way that pharmaceutical marketplaces operate, in the vast mess of the medical-industrial-government complex. It’s a problem so diffuse that it hardly makes sense to gather it all into one coherent encyclopedia entry.
The process by which the rest of the world influences the direction of an industry, by way of purchasing, analyzing, regulating, discussing, etc., is Selection. This comes from the terminology of evolution – in this framing, dinosaurs didn’t just decide to start growing wings and flying; Nature selected birds to fill the new ecological niches of the Jurassic period.
While Nature can’t do its selection on ethical grounds, we can, and do, when we select what kinds of companies and rules and power centers are filling which niches in our world. It’s a decentralized operation (like evolution), not controlled by any single entity, but consisting of the “sum total of the wills of the masses,” as Tolstoy put it.
The technical AI alignment problems (represented by the planets in the meme) are surely important, but what happens outside of the lab is just much bigger; AI is a small portion of the world economy; and yet AI touches almost all of us. The ways we select
how
AI touches us is, I want to suggest, the Big Question of AI Alignment. If you do care about AI Alignment in general, it’s a folly to ignore it.
In defense, a Selection-denier could argue that there is no progress to be made in directing the “sum total of the wills of the masses” towards the “group’s intended goals, preferences, or ethical principles.” But that would amount to rejecting the
Categorical Imperative
, and all the fun (and often very mathy) problems in game theory, and giving up on humanity, and only losers do that.
One sociotechnical protocol that can be applied to improving Selection efficiency is here:
https://muldoon.cloud/2025/03/08/civic-organizing.html
. But there are many others. This is the big work of AI Alignment. The meme said so.

data.title: Kangaroo: A flash cache optimized for tiny objects (2021)
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: Kangaroo是一种新的闪存缓存设计，旨在更高效地缓存微小对象（约100字节或更小），并解决了现有闪存缓存设计中的挑战。它通过CacheLib的API实现，开发者可利用其构建自定义缓存服务。Kangaroo结合了日志结构和组相联缓存，减少了DRAM和闪存写入开销，分为KLog（小容量日志结构缓存）和KSet（大容量组相联缓存）。其创新之处在于通过预先从KLog中移除对象，减少KSet的写放大效应。实验表明，Kangaroo在现实系统限制下减少了29%的缓存未命中率。该研究与卡内基梅隆大学合作，并在SOSP 2021会议上获得最佳论文奖。

44065299.article_content:
By
Sathya Gunasekar
,
Jimmy Lu
What the research is:
Kangaroo is a new flash cache that enables more efficient caching of tiny objects (objects that are ~100 bytes or less) and overcomes the challenges presented by existing flash cache designs. Since Kangaroo is implemented within
CacheLib
, Facebook’s open source caching engine, developers can use Kangaroo through CacheLib’s API to build their own customized cache services.
We partnered with Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) on this research. The resulting paper won the Best Paper award at the 2021
Symposium on Operating Systems Principles
(SOSP) conference.
CacheLib’s API allows developers to build and customize concurrent caches.
Optimized for tiny objects, Kangaroo minimizes dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) usage and the number of writes — and introduces a new cache eviction policy that reduces cache misses with minimal DRAM overhead, further reducing load on back-end storage systems.
Kangaroo’s CacheLib implementation also allowed our researchers to quickly evaluate the impact of Kangaroo’s design on real world production workloads. We evaluated Kangaroo using traces from production social graph caching workloads at Facebook and Twitter. Our experiments show Kangaroo reduces misses by 29 percent under realistic system constraints (DRAM and write rate constraints) compared with prior, state-of-the-art flash cache designs. These results are corroborated with a test deployment of Kangaroo in a shadow production setup.
Miss ratio for all three systems over a seven-day Facebook trace. Kangaroo reduces cache misses by 29 percent versus set-associative (SA) caches and by 56 percent versus log-structured (LS) caches.
How it works:
Current flash caches fall into two main categories: set-associative caches and log-structured caches. Set-associative caches write many more bytes than necessary because they have to write a 4 KB flash page — the minimum write granularity — for every object. With tiny objects that are roughly 100 bytes or less in size, this leads to significant write amplification (i.e., set-associative caches write ~40x more bytes than strictly necessary).
Log-structured caches have a large DRAM overhead because they have to keep an index entry for every on-flash object. Thus, neither set-associative nor log-structured flash caches are well designed for tiny object flash caches.
Kangaroo combines log-structured and set-associative caches to reduce both DRAM and flash-write overheads. Kangaroo has two main parts: KLog, a small log-structured flash cache, and KSet, a large set-associative flash cache.
Lookups first check the DRAM cache (1). If the object is not in the DRAM cache, requests check KLog’s index (2a) and then read the object from flash if the object was found in the index (2b). Requests finally check the per-set Bloom filter in KSet (3a) and read the set if the object could be in KSet (3b).
For inserts, Kangaroo first inserts objects into the DRAM cache (1). Objects evicted from the DRAM cache are either dropped by a preflash admission policy (2a) or added to KLog’s DRAM index (2b) and appended to KLog’s flash log (2c). Objects evicted from Klog are either dropped by another admission policy (3a) or inserted to KSet (3b).
One of Kangaroo’s innovations is in how it moves objects from KLog to KSet. Kangaroo uses KLog to find multiple objects mapping to the same set in KSet, such as the pink and yellow objects shown above. Whenever an object is evicted from KLog, Kangaroo proactively evicts objects from KLog to minimize write amplification in KSet.
Since writing a set always requires writing 4 KB, regardless of the number of objects inserted, writing two objects instead of just one cuts the write overhead per object in half. Thus, Kangaroo can amortize writes to KSet over multiple objects, decreasing the overall number of bytes written to flash. KLog accomplishes this goal with a small capacity (~5 percent of flash), so Kangaroo needs only a small amount of DRAM to index KLog’s entire capacity. Thus, Kangaroo addresses both the DRAM and flash-write overheads of caching tiny objects on flash.
On top of this basic design, Kangaroo introduces additional techniques to realize its hierarchical design and increase its effectiveness. In particular, since Kangaroo is a cache and not a key-value store, it can evict objects to minimize writes. Kangaroo exploits this opportunity by adding a threshold admission policy that evicts objects instead of admitting them to KSet if there are fewer than n objects to insert from KLog. This admission policy allows Kangaroo to guarantee that the write overhead for moving objects to KSet will be much lower than a set-associative cache. Kangaroo provides further optimizations to reduce DRAM overhead and reduce misses, as explained in our
SOSP 2021 paper
.
Together, these optimizations allow Kangaroo to overcome the limitations of log-structured caches and set-associative caches, creating a flash cache that delivers

data.title: Async from scratch 3: Pinned against the wall
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文主要讨论Rust中的`Future` trait及其相关概念，特别是**关联类型（associated types）**的用法和重要性。文章首先对比了`Future`和`SimpleFuture`两个trait，解释了关联类型与泛型的区别：关联类型类似于函数的返回值，而泛型则类似于函数的参数。接着，文章通过代码示例展示了如何正确实现关联类型，并说明了错误实现会导致的冲突问题。

文章进一步解释了关联类型的好处，包括提升类型推断的准确性和简化泛型代码的书写。随后，文章转向实际应用，展示如何将`async`函数转换为状态机和自定义的`Future`实现，并通过“不给糖就捣蛋”的示例详细说明如何实现相关的`Future`逻辑。

总结来说，本文的核心是解释Rust中`Future` trait的关联类型，并通过具体示例帮助读者理解如何正确使用和实现它。

44066237.article_summary:
本文主要讨论Rust中的`Future` trait及其相关概念，特别是**关联类型（associated types）**的用法和重要性。文章首先对比了`Future`和`SimpleFuture`两个trait，解释了关联类型与泛型的区别：关联类型类似于函数的返回值，而泛型则类似于函数的参数。接着，文章通过代码示例展示了如何正确实现关联类型，并说明了错误实现会导致的冲突问题。

文章进一步解释了关联类型的好处，包括提升类型推断的准确性和简化泛型代码的书写。随后，文章转向实际应用，展示如何将`async`函数转换为状态机和自定义的`Future`实现，并通过“不给糖就捣蛋”的示例详细说明如何实现相关的`Future`逻辑。

总结来说，本文的核心是解释Rust中`Future` trait的关联类型，并通过具体示例帮助读者理解如何正确使用和实现它。

data.article_summary: Glitch创始人Anil Dash宣布了一项重要更新：Glitch将于2025年7月8日停止为应用程序提供网页托管服务，用户配置文件和项目托管将关闭。尽管用户的控制面板和代码下载将保留至2025年底，且将新增重定向功能以保持链接有效，但平台将不再专注于托管应用。此决定主要出于运行成本增加及新平台兴起带来的生态变化。Glitch将专注于服务开发者社区的其他需求，并提供迁移指南和支持。现有Glitch Pro订阅将持续至7月8日，未使用时间将退款。此次变革虽具挑战，但团队承诺会妥善处理，并感谢社区的支持与理解。

44064230.article_content:
By
Anil Dash
May 22, 2025
Important Changes are Coming to Glitch
Today, I sent out an email to the Glitch community, and I wanted to include it here for everyone to reference, because it’s an important milestone for the community. This is a big change, but it’s not an “Our Incredible Journey” post about how our corporate overlords made us shut down the app hosting infrastructure for Glitch. It’s a story about recognizing when an ecosystem has changed, and evolving to reflect reality, and to respect our users and community by making the right choices when it’s time. As bittersweet as it is, this is a choice I stand behind, and I also am thinking deeply about what the Glitch community becomes, and what it means, going forward.
I hope you’ll share your thoughts about that topic, too. Either in the forum here, or by emailing me at
[email protected]
. I’m still as inspired as ever by seeing what you all create.
-Anil
We’ve got an important update for the Glitch community today: We’ll be ending web hosting for your apps on Glitch. In this message, we’ll explain what that means for you and for the Glitch community.
On July 8, 2025 Glitch project hosting and user profiles will be shut down. Your Glitch dashboard will remain available as usual through the end of 2025, with access to download all of your code for your projects, as well as a new feature to set up redirects for your project subdomains so your URLs keep working.
There are a couple of reasons we’re making this decision right now. It takes a lot of time and money to run millions of apps, and that has greatly increased as the platform has gotten older and bad actors try to misuse the platform. But while that is true, there’s also another motivation that made it clear that it’s time for a bigger change.
In the last few years, we’ve seen a lot of amazing new platforms that have raised the bar on how we create and run apps, just as Glitch first did almost a decade ago. Some of the teams behind these new platforms have even told us they were inspired by Glitch. ❤️ We love what we built with our teammates with Fastly Compute and tools like Fastly Fiddle, of course, but there’s also the broader ecosystem, with platforms like Fly.io, Deno, GitHub Pages, Val Town, Netlify, Digital Ocean, and so many more that are still inspiring us to create. Last year, we built the ability for paid Glitch members to share their own apps that they built elsewhere on their Glitch profiles, and we’ll be exploring how we might be able to revisit those kinds of ideas with the Glitch community going forward. So with so many good options for easily making and running apps, Glitch’s legacy architecture hasn’t been providing something uniquely valuable to the developer ecosystem at this point, and we want to focus our efforts on serving our developer community where we can be most valuable.
Right now, our number one job is to take care of everyone in the Glitch community during this big change. Here’s what we’re doing first:
Your Glitch dashboard will be available through the end of 2025 with code downloads for all of your projects
In the coming days, your dashboard will get a new feature to set up redirects for your project subdomains, so all your links will keep working. Make sure your redirects are set up before December 31, 2025. (We’ll make sure they stay active at least through the end of 2026.)
We’re working on preparing a guide to help you export your project, create git repos, and migrate your projects to new platforms. And we expect to update the guide as our friends at other platforms make it easy to move your projects over to their sites. Until then, please join us in the
Community Forum
to ask questions and get tips on migrating.
We’ll turn off new Glitch Pro subscriptions effective immediately. All current Glitch Pro subscriptions will be honored until July 8, and we’ll issue refunds for unused time. We’ll send a separate email to Glitch Pro subscribers with additional details on your membership by June 2, 2025.
This is obviously a big change for Glitch, and for the Glitch community. I know that personally, it’s a bittersweet transition, and any time we ask people to make an unexpected change with their apps, it can cause stress or frustration. I’m sorry for the time and effort that it takes to migrate or back up your apps if you weren’t planning on it, but I am also grateful for all the kind and supportive words from the community who’ve seen the challenges we’ve had in maintaining a large community of millions of users running tens of millions of apps.
We’ll keep updating you on progress towards these dates, and as always, you can join us in the community forum to share your thoughts or feedback and we’ll be watching closely. You can also personally reach out to me at
[email protected]
.
Thank you for being part of the Glitch community.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在编程中的作用及其与过去技术（如垃圾回收机制）的比较

不同观点：
• **tikhonj的观点**：当前的AI并没有真正减轻繁琐的工作，反而让低质量代码变得更加廉价和普遍，导致更多的负面外部效应。同时，对Java企业代码的看法与作者不同，表明价值观和美学上的差异。

• **NAHWheatCracker的观点**：不认同将垃圾回收与AI类比。垃圾回收让开发者无需关心内存问题，而AI则常常需要开发者去理解和修正其行为，且AI的行为不可预测，带来的问题比好处多。

• **npalli的观点**：Java在AI和机器学习浪潮中已经不再占据主导地位，编程语言的演变并没有一个统一的向更高抽象层次发展的故事。当前的技术发展呈现出多样化的趋势。

• **chr15m的观点**：AI是一个新的工具，可以提高生产力，但理解旧有的技术（如内存管理）仍然非常重要，能够让开发者更好地使用新工具。技术的进步往往建立在对过去知识的掌握上。

• **0x445442的观点**：JVM和垃圾回收机制并非Java独创，早期的Lisp和Smalltalk已经存在。对于他来说，Java的真正价值在于没有头文件和Javadoc，而不是垃圾回收。

• **leecommamichael的观点**：AI主要是一个更好的搜索工具，可以帮助开发者更快地找到解决方案，但开发者仍然掌握最终的决定权。相比于垃圾回收，AI是一个更有用且不那么侵入的工具。

• **ChrisMarshallNY的观点**：Java引入了许多设计模式和语言习惯用语，影响了后来的语言如Swift。当前的AI技术正处于一个不太讨人喜欢的阶段，但未来几年的新工具将会非常酷。AI不会取代所有开发者，只是给他们提供新的工具。

• **redwood的观点**：技术发展会带来新的可能性和新的做法，这是一个自然的演变过程。

• **keybored的观点**：对将AI与真正的抽象（如垃圾回收）进行类比表示不满。AI并没有可靠地抽象掉任何东西，而是提供了杠杆作用，可能会以不均匀的方式帮助开发者。文章中对过去的回顾和对AI的吹捧是不必要的。同时，对经济和社会的未来发展持怀疑态度，认为技术专家应该更加务实和批判性地看待技术发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI是否真正减轻了开发者的负担，还是只是让低质量代码更加泛滥。
• 对AI和垃圾回收机制的类比存在不同看法，一部分人认为AI不可预测且带来更多问题，另一部分人则认为AI是一个有用的工具。
• 对技术发展的未来持不同态度，一部分人乐观地认为AI会带来新的工具和可能性，另一部分人则持怀疑和批判态度。

• RadiozRadioz认为，在项目初期快速原型设计和探索问题领域时充满激情，但一旦问题解决、路径明确后，剩下的实施工作会变得枯燥无味。他的大脑会自动寻找新的问题，而不是继续完成剩下的“按部就班”的任务。

• guywithahat指出，自己的副业项目通常没有社区参与，并建议那些寻找项目的人可以尝试联系那些已经停止更新但仍有待解决问题的老项目作者。

• achieve_freedom表示自己有一个曾赚到少量钱的iOS应用，但由于缺乏在特定领域的知识，无法有效营销。他更关注当前的新项目，并询问其他人具体在寻找什么样的项目。

• rasulkireev认为自己很幸运能够自托管项目，这样在厌倦一个项目时可以轻松停止，不必担心服务切换，因为所有基础设施都是自己搭建的，项目可以自主运行。

• whatamidoingyo直接询问是否有人打算购买项目，表现出对项目交易的兴趣。

• busymom0提到自己开发的一个生产力应用难以获得关注和下载，尽管进行了多次优化和推广尝试。她对是否放弃这个项目感到犹豫。

补充讨论：
• 项目厌倦感：RadiozRadioz描述了一种在解决问题后失去兴趣的心理现象，这可能是许多开发者在项目中后期遇到的常见问题。

• 项目营销与推广：busymom0和achieve_freedom都提到了项目营销的挑战，尤其是如何有效推广和吸引用户，这是许多独立开发者面临的难题。

• 项目社区与合作：guywithahat建议寻找有社区支持的项目，强调了社区在项目持续发展中的重要性。

• 项目自主性与可持续性：rasulkireev强调自托管项目的好处，即在项目完成后无需持续干预，能够自主运行，减轻了开发者的负担。

争议焦点：
• 项目的后期实施工作是否枯燥：RadiozRadioz认为项目后期的工作缺乏吸引力，而rasulkireev则表示如果项目能够自主运行，就可以轻松摆脱项目负担，暗示后期工作不一定是问题。这体现出开发者对项目不同阶段的感受和处理方式的差异。

data.title: Launch HN: SIM Studio (YC X25) – Figma-Like Canvas for Agent Workflows
data.author: waleedlatif1
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SimStudio产品的功能、定位、用户体验及其与竞争对手的比较。

不同观点：
• [manish_sg] 关注SimStudio是否支持在SaaS中嵌入多租户部署。他认为这是一个关键问题，因为这涉及到产品的应用场景和适用性。

• [matt3D] 对编配工具的用户体验（UX）提出了批评，认为这些工具没有优先考虑人工智能（AI）特性。他建议工具的首要功能应是帮助用户通过提示窗口搭建编配流程。

• [jasongill] 提到了SimStudio在市场上的竞争，并与其他具有AI功能的编配工具（如n8n和Rivet）进行比较。他希望看到SimStudio的独特之处和优势。

• [srameshc] 提供了关于产品主页的反馈，认为当前主页不足以清晰传达产品功能，建议参考GitHub上的GIF演示来改进网站说明。

• [primitivesuave] 对SimStudio的发布表示祝贺，并对团队快速迭代产品的能力表示赞赏。他特别提到SimStudio在React Flow方面的优秀表现。

• [flaviuspopan] 对SimStudio表示兴趣，但提出了两个实际问题：一是关于未来的定价策略，二是关于MCP服务器集成的可能性，以支持特定的业务需求。

• [worldsayshi] 认为像Figma/Excalidraw那样的画布解决方案在不同的问题领域中具有潜力，暗示这种交互方式可能适用于更多场景。

• [barbazoo] 建议增加更多实际案例，以便用户更好地理解产品的应用场景。

• [efitz] 将SimStudio比喻为“IFTTT for LLM agents”，暗示其功能类似于IFTTT，但专注于LLM（大型语言模型）代理。

• [Geep5] 表达了对编配工具空间（如Rivet）的喜爱，尤其是开源和免费的特性，使其编码体验更加愉快。

补充讨论：
• 用户对SimStudio的功能、用户体验和市场定位存在不同关注点，有人关注其技术实现（如MCP服务器集成），有人关注其市场竞争力及定价策略。
• 关于产品说明和用户引导的讨论表明用户对产品理解和使用便捷性的重视。
• 不同用户对产品优缺点的反馈揭示了SimStudio在市场中的潜在竞争点和改进方向。

data.title: 32 bits that changed microprocessor design
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了贝尔实验室的Bellmac-32微处理器，它是世界上首批32位微处理器之一，对现代智能手机芯片设计产生了深远影响。1982年，Bellmac-32团队在新泽西州莫瑞山的贝尔实验室完成了这一突破性设计。该芯片引入了32位架构，为后续更复杂、更高效的处理器奠定了基础。作者Willie D. Jones指出，Bellmac-32不仅提升了计算能力，还推动了微处理器设计的多项创新，最终促成了今天智能手机中使用的先进芯片技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bellmac-32处理器的技术特点、历史地位、未能普及的原因以及其独特指令集。

不同观点：
• [zik] 认为Bellmac-32在技术上受VAX-11/780架构影响很大，尤其是32位CPU、两级流水线和按需分页虚拟内存等特性，但Bellmac-32在CMOS技术上的成功应用是其独特贡献。他指出VAX系列因为LSI技术应用缓慢而逐渐被淘汰。
• [zahlman] 关注Bellmac-32未成为主流的原因，认为文章对此解释不足，并质疑AT&T选择其他方案的理由不够充分，指出像苹果从Xerox PARC获取灵感那样，其他公司本可以采用Bellmac-32的技术。
• [Findecanor] 注意到Bellmac-32指令集中的一个特殊指令'ASL'，其行为不同于常见的ISA，指出大多数ISA没有单独的算术和逻辑左移指令，并举M68K为例说明差异。
• [macshome] 表达了对Bell Labs历史贡献的敬佩，认为当今需要更多像Bell Labs这样的创新机构。
• [jandrese] 怀疑Bellmac-32未能成功的原因之一可能是成本问题，并提到8086处理器的竞争威胁。
• [willmarquis] 强调Bellmac-32在技术上的领先地位，尤其是在CMOS技术应用上的突破，但最终未能获得应有的市场成功，获得IEEE的里程碑更像是“终身成就奖”。
• [didgetmaster] 分享个人经历，提到自己1986年购买的AT&T 6300电脑使用的是Intel 8086处理器，间接说明Bellmac-32市场普及度不高。
• [rkagerer] 描述了Bellmac-32开发过程中的技术挑战，尤其是没有全芯片验证的CAD工具，团队通过手工绘制和物理组装来验证设计。
• [joezydeco] 分享了作为UIUC学生时使用Bellmac-32处理器的经历，认为其在C和汇编语言编程方面比Intel更有趣，并且具有独特的STRCPY操作码。

补充讨论：
• Bellmac-32在技术上的创新与其市场失败之间的矛盾是讨论的焦点之一，尤其是在与VAX和8086的竞争背景下。
• 不同的评论者从技术细节、历史背景、个人体验和市场角度分析了Bellmac-32的成败原因，展现了多维度的讨论。

data.title: The Future of Flatpak
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Flatpak项目的现状与未来。尽管Flatpak在应用打包格式上取得了一定成功，受到开发者和用户欢迎，且被Fedora等Linux发行版采用，但其核心开发进展缓慢。演讲者Sebastian Wick指出，虽然项目维护和安全修复仍在进行，但缺乏对新功能的审查和重大更新。关键开发者的离开导致代码合并过程延迟，新的贡献者也难以快速融入。此外，Wick提到OSTree工具的局限性，并建议采用OCI图像工具以简化开发流程。总体而言，Flatpak功能稳定，但发展受到制约，未来需要更多开发者参与以推动创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flatpak项目的现状、其设计和实用性以及与其他软件打包机制的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flatpak开发停滞**：ndiddy和OsrsNeedsf2P指出，Flatpak项目看似成功，但实际上已经停滞不前，缺乏重大更新。OsrsNeedsf2P特别提到，他曾对Flatpak充满期待，但随着时间的推移，开发活动减少，导致他逐渐失去兴趣。

• **权限问题和兼容性不足**：ndiddy、conradev和amluto提到Flatpak在权限管理上的问题，比如无法为特定功能（如创建虚拟接口）设置权限。amluto还批评了Flatpak在应用程序实例权限管理上的设计缺陷，认为其无法有效隔离不同实例的权限。

• **与其他打包机制的比较**：mrbluecoat和sabslikesobs认为AppImage和传统包管理系统更具优势。mrbluecoat特别提到AppImage的便携性和用户友好性。sabslikesobs则表示，虽然转向Flatpak基础的不变发行版有其优势，但也遇到了许多不稳定和兼容性问题。

• **社区和生态系统支持不足**：bee_rider和sohrob提到Flatpak社区的参与度不高，以及开源社区未能集中资源改进Flatpak。sohrob特别指出，面对众多Linux发行版，社区未能合力推动一个统一的解决方案。

• **设计哲学和整体生态的批评**：zbentley对Flatpak及其他打包工具在Linux生态中的位置进行了深刻批评，认为这些工具虽然在一定程度上解决了应用分发问题，但同时也引入了复杂性和安全问题。ggm则从历史角度分析，认为当前的分裂状态是不可避免的。

补充讨论：
• **具体使用问题**：dbolgheroni分享了在使用Flatpak安装VSCode/Codium时遇到的调试问题，最终转向Snap解决。SubiculumCode也提到在使用Flatpak和Snap时遇到不一致行为和权限错误的问题。

• **对特定发行版的影响**：tomrod关注Flatpak问题对Fedora等发行版的潜在影响，显示出对整体生态健康状况的担忧。

争议焦点：Flatpak是否应由Red Hat等大公司提供更多资源支持以维持其发展，以及是否应集中社区力量推动一个统一的Linux桌面应用分发方案。

(LAS) in April, Sebastian Wick said that, by many metrics,
Flatpak
is doing great. The Flatpak
application-packaging format is popular with upstream developers, and
with many users. More and more applications are being published in the
Flathub
application store, and the
format is even being adopted by Linux distributions like
Fedora. However, he worried that work on the Flatpak project itself
had stagnated, and that there were too few developers able to review
and merge code beyond basic maintenance.
I was not able to attend LAS in person or watch it live-streamed,
so I watched the YouTube
video
of the
talk. The slides are available from the
talk
page
. Wick is a member of the GNOME Project and a Red Hat employee
who works on "
all kinds of desktop plumbing
", including Flatpak
and
desktop
portals
.
Flatpak basics
Flatpak was
originally
developed
by Alexander Larsson, who had been working on similar
projects stretching back to 2007. The
first
release
was as XDG-App in 2015. It was renamed to Flatpak in 2016,
a nod to IKEA's "
flatpacks
"
for delivering furniture.
The Flatpak project provides
command-line
tools
for managing and running Flatpak applications, tools for
building
Flatpak bundles
, and
runtimes
that provide components for Flatpak applications. The project uses
control groups
,
namespaces
,
bind mounts
,
seccomp
, and
Bubblewrap
to provide application isolation ("sandboxing"). Flatpak content is
primarily delivered using
OSTree
,
though support for using
Open
Container Initiative (OCI) images
has been
available
since 2018 and is used by Fedora for its Flatpak applications. The "
Under
the Hood
" page from Flatpak's documentation provides a good
overview of how the pieces fit together.
Slowing development
Wick started his talk by saying that it looks like everything is
great with the Flatpak project, but if one looks deeper, "
you will
notice that it's not being actively developed anymore
". There are
people who maintain the code base and fix security issues, for
example, but "
bigger changes are not really happening
anymore
". He said that there are a bunch of merge requests for new
features, but no one feels responsible for reviewing them, and that is
kind of problematic.
$ sudo subscribe today
Subscribe today and elevate your LWN privileges. You’ll have
access to all of LWN’s high-quality articles as soon as they’re
published, and help support LWN in the process.
Act now
and you can start with a free trial subscription.
The reason for the lack of reviewers is that key people, such as
Larsson, have left the project. Every now and then, Wick said, Larsson
may get involved if it's necessary, but he is basically not part of
the day-to-day development of the project. Wick said that it is hard
to get new Flatpak contributors involved because it can take months to
get feedback on major changes, and then more months to get another
review. "
This is really not a great way to get someone up to speed,
and it's not a great situation to be in
."
"
Maybe I'm complaining about something that is actually not that
much of an issue
", he said. Flatpak works; it does its job, and
"
we just use it and don't think about it much
". In that sense,
the project is in a good spot. But he has still been thinking
about how the project is "
living with constraints
" because
contributors do not have the opportunity to go in and make bigger
changes.
As an example, Wick said that Red Hat has been doing work that
would allow Flatpaks to be installed as part of a base
installation. The vendor or administrator could specify the
applications to be installed, and a program called
flatpak-preinstall
would take care of the rest. The feature
has been implemented and is planned for inclusion in Red Hat
Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 10. The work was
started
by
Kalev Lember and Owen Taylor last June, but the original pull request
was
closed
by Lember in February as he was leaving Red Hat and would not be
working on it anymore. It was picked up by Wick in February as a
new request
but wasn't reviewed until early May.
OSTree and OCI
Wick's next topic was OCI support in Flatpak. While OSTree has been
a success in some ways, and it is still being maintained, it is not
undergoing active development. He noted that developers have a
"
very narrow set of tools
" for working with OSTree, so building
Flatpaks that use OSTree requires non-standard and bespoke tools, but
there is a whole range of utilities available for working with OCI
images. Even better, tools for working with OCI images "
are all
developed by people other than us, which means we don't actually have
to do the work if we just embrace them
".

44068400.article_summary: 本文讨论了Flatpak项目的现状与未来。尽管Flatpak在应用打包格式上取得了一定成功，受到开发者和用户欢迎，且被Fedora等Linux发行版采用，但其核心开发进展缓慢。演讲者Sebastian Wick指出，虽然项目维护和安全修复仍在进行，但缺乏对新功能的审查和重大更新。关键开发者的离开导致代码合并过程延迟，新的贡献者也难以快速融入。此外，Wick提到OSTree工具的局限性，并建议采用OCI图像工具以简化开发流程。总体而言，Flatpak功能稳定，但发展受到制约，未来需要更多开发者参与以推动创新。

主要讨论点：Flatpak项目的现状、其设计和实用性以及与其他软件打包机制的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flatpak开发停滞**：ndiddy和OsrsNeedsf2P指出，Flatpak项目看似成功，但实际上已经停滞不前，缺乏重大更新。OsrsNeedsf2P特别提到，他曾对Flatpak充满期待，但随着时间的推移，开发活动减少，导致他逐渐失去兴趣。

• **权限问题和兼容性不足**：ndiddy、conradev和amluto提到Flatpak在权限管理上的问题，比如无法为特定功能（如创建虚拟接口）设置权限。amluto还批评了Flatpak在应用程序实例权限管理上的设计缺陷，认为其无法有效隔离不同实例的权限。

• **与其他打包机制的比较**：mrbluecoat和sabslikesobs认为AppImage和传统包管理系统更具优势。mrbluecoat特别提到AppImage的便携性和用户友好性。sabslikesobs则表示，虽然转向Flatpak基础的不变发行版有其优势，但也遇到了许多不稳定和兼容性问题。

• **社区和生态系统支持不足**：bee_rider和sohrob提到Flatpak社区的参与度不高，以及开源社区未能集中资源改进Flatpak。sohrob特别指出，面对众多Linux发行版，社区未能合力推动一个统一的解决方案。

• **设计哲学和整体生态的批评**：zbentley对Flatpak及其他打包工具在Linux生态中的位置进行了深刻批评，认为这些工具虽然在一定程度上解决了应用分发问题，但同时也引入了复杂性和安全问题。ggm则从历史角度分析，认为当前的分裂状态是不可避免的。

补充讨论：
• **具体使用问题**：dbolgheroni分享了在使用Flatpak安装VSCode/Codium时遇到的调试问题，最终转向Snap解决。SubiculumCode也提到在使用Flatpak和Snap时遇到不一致行为和权限错误的问题。

• **对特定发行版的影响**：tomrod关注Flatpak问题对Fedora等发行版的潜在影响，显示出对整体生态健康状况的担忧。

争议焦点：Flatpak是否应由Red Hat等大公司提供更多资源支持以维持其发展，以及是否应集中社区力量推动一个统一的Linux桌面应用分发方案。

data.title: The copilot delusion
data.author: isaiahwp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件开发中的作用及其对开发者工作的影响

不同观点：
• Padolsey认为，对于大多数开发工作，软件开发并没有太多创新，主要是重复使用已有的代码模式。AI编码助手只是强化了这种代码重用，适用于构建常见的CRUD应用，但对于如导弹制导系统等高要求的软件开发，仍需深入学习和理解底层技术。
• Felubra对技术细节和底层硬件有深刻的情感，认为开发者应关注硬件细节，并欣赏与机器交互的美。
• Lunarcave指出，编写代码不仅是最终的产物，还包括在开发过程中所做的权衡。AI可以帮助编写代码，但思考和指导AI生成正确输出仍是人类的工作。
• CGamesPlay认为，过去工程师面临的技术挑战有其历史背景，当前依赖AI可能导致我们不断重复和强化过去30年中积累的技术债务，而非创新。
• Webprofusion将AI与初级开发者类比，认为AI可以完成部分工作，但仍需人工进行修正和优化，最终用户只关心系统功能而非代码质量。

补充讨论：
• Heddycrow以幽默方式表达对文章的共鸣。
• Jboggan担忧未来代码质量下降，因为LLM生成的代码可能冻结过去的错误和不良实践。
• Swyx认为，开发者应具备在不同抽象层次间切换的能力，既能高层次思考，也能深入细节修正代码。
• Malfist批评管理层对AI的不现实期望，认为AI仅在特定情况下有效，且可能导致忽视实际工作需求。
• Jcampuzano2强调，许多非技术人员只关注功能实现，不关心代码质量，这推动了AI在开发中的应用。若放弃对代码美学的追求，AI可能在当前状态下替代许多角色。
• Sgarland担忧AI让那些对技术无热情的人进入行业，类似于DevOps领域中因抽象工具而获得职位的人。
• Airstrike建议，在讨论AI辅助编码时，应明确编程语言、应用领域、使用的AI模型和交互界面，以避免无效讨论。
• Aziell分享了个人经验，指出过度依赖AI助手可能导致停止思考和成长。
• Wewewedxfgdf表达了对编程普及的开放态度。
• Tptacek以电子表格为例，指出对AI取代工作的担忧历史上已有类似讨论。

争议焦点：
• AI在软件开发中的实际作用和其对开发者职业成长的影响。
• 过度依赖AI可能导致代码质量下降与技术债务累积。
• 管理层对AI不切实际的期望和对开发工作的影响。

data.title: Show HN: Defuddle, an HTML-to-Markdown alternative to Readability
data.author: kepano
data.article_summary: Defuddle是一个用于从网页中提取主要内容的工具，能够去除不必要的元素如评论、侧边栏、页眉、页脚等，生成干净、可读的HTML文档。它专为Obsidian Web Clipper设计，适合作为Mozilla Readability的替代品，具有更宽容的元素处理方式，并能一致地处理脚注、代码块等。Defuddle提供三个版本：核心版（无依赖，适合浏览器使用）、完整版（支持数学公式解析）、Node.js版（使用JSDOM，支持Markdown转换）。它提取的内容包括标题、作者、发布日期、主图、网站图标等元数据，并提供调试模式和选择性移除元素的功能。安装通过npm进行，使用时可根据需求配置选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于网页内容提取工具的实现、使用场景及相关技术选择的讨论

不同观点：
• [ulrischa] 分享了自己使用PHP构建的类似工具，强调了其易于自托管的特点。
• [tmpfs] 提到不同语言的Readability实现质量参差不齐，推荐了Python的trifatura库，认为其在内容提取和元数据准确性上表现更好，建议与现有实现进行比较以寻求改进。
• [acrophobic] 质疑Mozilla的Readability被遗弃的说法，指出其最新版本发布于两个月前，且维护者活跃地回应问题。
• [Andr2Andr] 提出疑问，询问这种工具的实际使用场景，仅在其他评论中看到用于导出ChatGPT对话为Markdown的例子。
• [jeanlucas] 回应了使用场景的问题，确认Obsidian Web Clipper可用于将ChatGPT对话转换为Markdown或直接打印。
• [revskill] 指出Markdown不支持表单元素，暗示了工具在某些功能上的局限性。
• [billconan] 询问工具是否在后台使用AI模型（如Gemini），以理解使用成本对比Readability。

补充讨论：
• [timdeve] 表示计划尝试将RSS阅读器的可读性功能替换为该工具，并提到由于Pocket即将关闭，可能需要添加“稍后阅读”功能。
• [Tsarp] 对Obsidian Clipper的网站个性化内容提取功能表示赞赏，认为其Markdown提取质量最为可靠。
• [creakingstairs] 提到在研究Obsidian Web Clipper的源码时发现了Defuddle，并计划用于自己的读取和知识库应用。
• [jonplackett] 提问为何某些网站在iPhone的阅读器模式下显示空白页，怀疑是网站故意设置障碍以保护广告收入。
• [rcarmo] 分享了自己多年前实现的Readability算法的经验，最终选择了Python的替代方案，并指出这些工具在定期更新中表现良好。
• [inhumantsar] 提到Readability处于“生命支持”状态，曾参与的Obsidian插件Slurp在维护上遇到困难，尽管如此，Slurp仍不断吸引新用户。

争议焦点：
• Readability的现状及其是否被遗弃。
• 网页内容提取工具在不同网站上的兼容性问题及其背后的技术原因。

总体而言，讨论围绕网页内容提取工具的技术实现、使用场景、兼容性问题及其背后的技术选型展开。

de·​fud·dle /diˈfʌdl/
transitive verb
to remove unnecessary elements from a web page, and make it easily readable.
Beware! Defuddle is very much a work in progress!
Defuddle extracts the main content from web pages. It cleans up web pages by removing clutter like comments, sidebars, headers, footers, and other non-essential elements, leaving only the primary content.
Try the Defuddle Playground →
Features
Defuddle aims to output clean and consistent HTML documents. It was written for
Obsidian Web Clipper
with the goal of creating a more useful input for HTML-to-Markdown converters like
Turndown
.
Defuddle can be used as a replacement for
Mozilla Readability
with a few differences:
More forgiving, removes fewer uncertain elements.
Provides a consistent output for footnotes, math, code blocks, etc.
Uses a page's mobile styles to guess at unnecessary elements.
Extracts more metadata from the page, including schema.org data.
Installation
npm install defuddle
For Node.js usage, you'll also need to install JSDOM:
npm install jsdom
Usage
Browser
import
{
Defuddle
}
from
'defuddle'
;
// Parse the current document
const
defuddle
=
new
Defuddle
(
document
)
;
const
result
=
defuddle
.
parse
(
)
;
// Access the content and metadata
console
.
log
(
result
.
content
)
;
console
.
log
(
result
.
title
)
;
console
.
log
(
result
.
author
)
;
Node.js
import
{
JSDOM
}
from
'jsdom'
;
import
{
Defuddle
}
from
'defuddle/node'
;
// Parse HTML from a string
const
html
=
'<html><body><article>...</article></body></html>'
;
const
result
=
await
Defuddle
(
html
)
;
// Parse HTML from a URL
const
dom
=
await
JSDOM
.
fromURL
(
'https://example.com/article'
)
;
const
result
=
await
Defuddle
(
dom
)
;
// With options
const
result
=

Defuddle
(

,
{

:

,
// Enable debug mode for verbose logging

:

:
'https://example.com/article'
// Original URL of the page
}
)
;
// Access the content and metadata
console

)

)

)
;
Note: for
defuddle/node
to import properly, the module format in your
package.json
has to be set to
{ "type": "module" }
Response
Defuddle returns an object with the following properties:
Property
Type
Description
author
string
Author of the article
content
string
Cleaned up string of the extracted content
description
string
Description or summary of the article
domain
string
Domain name of the website
favicon
string
URL of the website's favicon
image
string
URL of the article's main image
metaTags
object
Meta tags
parseTime
number
Time taken to parse the page in milliseconds
published
string
Publication date of the article
site
string
Name of the website
schemaOrgData
object
Raw schema.org data extracted from the page
title
string
Title of the article
wordCount
number
Total number of words in the extracted content
Bundles
Defuddle is available in three different bundles:
Core bundle (
defuddle
): The main bundle for browser usage. No dependencies.
Full bundle (
defuddle/full
): Includes additional features for math equation parsing.
Node.js bundle (
defuddle/node
): Optimized for Node.js environments using JSDOM. Includes full capabilities for math and Markdown conversion.
The core bundle is recommended for most use cases. It still handles math content, but doesn't include fallbacks for converting between MathML and LaTeX formats. The full bundle adds the ability to create reliable
<math>
elements using
mathml-to-latex
and
temml
libraries.
Options
Option
Type
Description
debug
boolean
Enable debug logging
url
string
URL of the page being parsed
markdown
boolean
Convert
content
to Markdown
separateMarkdown
boolean
Keep
content
as HTML and return
contentMarkdown
as Markdown
removeExactSelectors
boolean
Whether to remove elements matching exact selectors like ads, social buttons, etc. Defaults to true.
removePartialSelectors
boolean
Whether to remove elements matching partial selectors like ads, social buttons, etc. Defaults to true.

44067409.article_summary: Defuddle是一个用于从网页中提取主要内容的工具，能够去除不必要的元素如评论、侧边栏、页眉、页脚等，生成干净、可读的HTML文档。它专为Obsidian Web Clipper设计，适合作为Mozilla Readability的替代品，具有更宽容的元素处理方式，并能一致地处理脚注、代码块等。Defuddle提供三个版本：核心版（无依赖，适合浏览器使用）、完整版（支持数学公式解析）、Node.js版（使用JSDOM，支持Markdown转换）。它提取的内容包括标题、作者、发布日期、主图、网站图标等元数据，并提供调试模式和选择性移除元素的功能。安装通过npm进行，使用时可根据需求配置选项。

data.title: Airport for DuckDB
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: "Airport"扩展为DuckDB增加了Arrow Flight支持，使其能够通过Arrow Flight服务器查询、修改和存储数据。Arrow Flight是一种基于Apache Arrow的高性能数据服务框架，允许DuckDB访问非表格数据、外部API以及自定义SQL函数，并提供远程执行的用户自定义函数（UDFs）和细粒度的数据访问控制。通过该扩展，DuckDB可以实现原本无法完成的数据服务功能。安装该社区扩展需运行`INSTALL airport FROM community;`和`LOAD airport;`命令。该扩展还支持构建Arrow Flight服务器，并在DuckCon #6会议上进行了介绍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DuckDB的功能、优势、局限性以及在实际应用中的使用场景。

不同观点：
• mrbungie：对DuckDB总体持积极评价，认为它是跨平台的强大分析引擎，但对其不支持Iceberg写入感到失望，认为这会增加技术栈的复杂性，需要额外的引擎来处理插入操作。
• r3tr0：非常喜欢DuckDB，并分享了他们在eBPF数据处理中的实际应用，提供了一个沙盒环境来展示其用途。
• k_bx：关注DuckDB是否支持加载IPC文件，因为这是他们在将数据转换为Parquet文件之前进行追加操作的重要需求。
• vkaku：赞赏DuckDB及其相关工具（如fuzzycomplete和lindel）的功能，表现出对DuckDB生态系统的喜爱。
• rubenvanwyk：关心数据源和目标是否都需要设置Flight服务器，并质疑这种方法在与第三方服务集成时的实用性。
• blef：认为DuckDB及其相关功能是一个有趣的思想实验，可以实现所有数据处理任务都通过SQL完成，将其比作MCPs（主控程序）在DuckDB世界中的表现。

补充讨论：
• the_optimist：质疑这种方法的实际应用场景，认为需要明确解释在什么情况下这种方案是最佳解决方案，尤其是在替代远程DuckDB实例和DB服务器的情况下。
• 对Iceberg写入支持的缺乏（mrbungie提出）和IPC文件加载问题（k_bx提出）是两个主要的技术限制，可能影响用户的技术选型。
• 对DuckDB实际应用的讨论，如r3tr0提供的系统级指标处理案例，展示了其在特定领域的成功应用。

争议焦点：DuckDB在处理复杂数据操作（如Iceberg写入和IPC文件处理）时的能力不足，以及其在实际应用场景中的适用性问题（the_optimist的观点）。

44028616.article_content:
The
Airport
extension brings
Arrow Flight
support to
DuckDB
, enabling DuckDB to query, modify, and store data via Arrow Flight servers. A DuckDB extension is a plugin that expands DuckDBâs core functionality by adding new capabilities.
To understand the rationale behind the development of this extension, check out the
motivation for creating the extension
.
Getting started
The Airport extension is a
DuckDB community extension
. To install it, run the following SQL inside DuckDB:
INSTALL airport
FROM
community;
To load the extension you can then execute:
LOAD airport;
If you wish to build the extension from source see these
instructions
.
What can I do with the Airport extension that I canât do with DuckDB now?
With the Airport extension you can:
Query data that DuckDB canât normally accessâeither because itâs non-tabular or in an unsupported format. Even external APIs. It all depends what the server allows.
Add custom
scalar
or
table returning
SQL functions not available in DuckDB.
Provide User Defined Functions (UDFs) for DuckDB that execute remotely.
Serve data with fine-grained access control, filtering both rows and columns based on user permissions.
Access and provide
Data-as-a-Service
.
What is Arrow Flight?
From the Apache Arrow Documentation:
Arrow Flight
is an RPC framework for high-performance data services based on
Apache Arrow
and is built on top of
gRPC
and the
Arrow IPC format
.
Flight is organized around streams of Arrow record batches
1
, being either downloaded from or uploaded to another service. A set of metadata methods offers discovery and introspection of streams, as well as the ability to implement application-specific methods.
Methods and message wire formats are defined by
Protobuf
, enabling interoperability with clients that may support gRPC and Arrow separately, but not Flight. However, Flight implementations include further optimizations to avoid overhead in usage of Protobuf (mostly around avoiding excessive memory copies).
What is an Apache Arrow âFlightâ?
An Apache Arrow flight (hereafter referred to simply as a âflightâ) is a source or destination for data that is accessible via the Apache Arrow Flight RPC framework. Each flight has a schema and one or more endpoints, that may offer one or more locations.
You can think of flights to be simliar to be a collection of files that share the same schema or even more apt a database table that is stored on a remote server. Apache Arrow Flight servers often provide many different flights.
How does Airport work with DuckDB?
Airport is an extension written in C++ for DuckDB version 1.3.0 or later, it utilizes the Apache Arrow library.
How can I build an Arrow Flight Server?
Start by reading the
basics of implementing an Arrow Flight Server
.
Conference Presentations
Rusty Conover presented the Airport extension in a presentation titled
âAirport For DuckDB: Letting DuckDB take flight.â
at DuckCon #6.
Footnotes
A record batch is a collection of equal-length arrays that all match a schema.

data.title: “Secret Mall Apartment,” a Protest for Place
data.author: rufus_foreman
data.article_summary: 《Secret Mall Apartment》讲述了2003年美国罗得岛的一群艺术家秘密栖居于一家繁忙购物中心，并在未经许可的情况下生活了约四年。他们在商场中一个无人注意的隐蔽空间里安家，利用旧货店的物品布置居所，以此抗议这座毫无生气的消费主义神殿。这群艺术家此前曾将废弃工厂改造成住家和艺术场所，但被开发项目驱逐。新建造的商场进一步分隔了城市中的贫富区域，激起了他们的反抗情绪。他们偶尔使用商场的公共设施，并通过建造墙壁隐藏住所，成功多年未被发现。这部纪录片通过他们的视角，揭示了对城市过度开发和现代消费文化的无声抗议。

44067767.article_content:
In 2003, a group of Rhode Island artists created a secret living space within a busy shopping mall and lived there off and on, undetected, for about four years.
Why?
The new documentary
Secret Mall Apartment
, now in select theaters nationwide, tells the story of eight Providence-based artists who, although they periodically hint at their left-leaning politics, admirably dedicate their time and skills to projects paying tribute to the first-responder firemen who perished on 9/11, the victims of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, and sick children in hospitals. It’s touching. You root for them.
Oh, and they live in their local mall.
Directed by Jeremy Workman and produced by actor Jesse Eisenberg, the documentary features grainy 2000s cell-phone camera footage of the cast of characters—all artists but also intimate friends—as well as modern-day interviews about their time living in the mall.
The ringleader is Michael Townsend, who is fifty-four now and hatched the mall apartment project in his early thirties. When the Providence Place Mall was under construction, one of Townsend’s friends noticed that there was an odd space that didn’t seem to have a dedicated purpose. Townsend took the lead on furnishing the space with goods from the Salvation Army and other thrift stores.
Townsend
said
in an interview, “It was windowless, lifeless concrete, very industrial, not designed to be comfortable in any way—that said, myself and my comrades are all repeat offenders of moving into mill spaces that are big and industrial and making them into our homes—that’s our whole bag.”
The original plan was to stay a week.
The latest essay every day.
Email
*
Sign Up
“It trains you to be in a mindset that you have a sort of role as steward of spaces that you will temporarily make something different and uniquely beautiful, and just as easily remove it,” he added.
The artists’ squatting was a statement. They hated the mall. By “living” there, without permission or anyone even noticing (the logistics of their apartment living are some of the most interesting parts of the movie) the artists attempt to domesticate and humanize this soulless shrine to consumerism foisted on them by city planners.
These Gen X and Millennial artists had only known late twentieth- and early twenty-first-century post-industrial Providence, and they made home out of the little they had to work with. They had repurposed abandoned textile mill buildings into apartments, art galleries, and warehouse party spots in an area known as Fort Thunder. Developers eventually demolished Fort Thunder, kicking the artists out. Not long after, developers began construction on the Providence Place Mall, which, seemingly by design, separated the working class areas of Providence from the wealthier areas. For many locals, it was a lot of development all at once, the mall in particular being a radical transformation for their city.
Deciding to squat in the mall they hated was a unique form of defiance against lifeless urban sprawl, but the sentiment was not exactly new. From the Southern Agrarians of the 1930s to Richard Weaver and beyond, there is a long history of conservative resistance to modernity, particularly the industrial revolution.
Watching the film, my mind first went to Russell Kirk and Wendell Berry and their
low opinion
of bulldozers, but even more so to the great localist conservative Bill Kauffman. Of his own often-mentioned and beloved hometown of Batavia, New York, Kauffman
wrote
in 2017, “Our city fathers rushed headlong into this mad program whereby the federal government paid Batavia to knock down its past: the mansions of the founders, sandstone churches, the brick shops of Main Street—the whole damned—or, rather, blessed—thing.”
“Batavia,” he continued, “tore out its five-block heart and filled the cavity with a ghastly mall, a colossal failure built in the aptly named Brutalist style. We are used today in urban-planning texts as a case study in disaster.”
Lamenting the mall and the demolition of old Batavia, Kauffman added, “In some ways we were a typical small American city but in other ways we were ‘Batavia’—our own place. We did not yet bow down before the new American royalty: Burger King and Dairy Queen.”
The tenants of
Secret Mall Apartment
frequented the mall food court of Burger Kings, Dairy Queens, or whatever interchangeable fast-food offerings were available. They used the public bathrooms. They built a cinder block wall to further conceal their hiding place, with each occupant having a key to the door, where they could enter at any time to play video games or spend the night.
It was meant as an unusual form of protest, only known to them. The same generic mall imposed on Providence, impervious to the organic customs and character of the place, was also detached enough from the human beings who lived there that the building’s authorities didn’t detect a gaggle of them inhabiting the property for four years.
How they are eventually discovered i

主要讨论点：对Richard Garwin和Theodore Hall的历史背景及其在核武器发展中的角色进行分析和讨论。

不同观点：
• **Hilift**的观点：强调Theodore Hall和Richard Garwin在同一时间都在芝加哥大学，且都是神童。Hilift详细介绍了Hall的间谍活动及其对苏联提供原子弹细节的文件，以及他在麦卡锡时代的调查中被保护的背景。Hilift认为Hall虽然涉及间谍活动，但仍被空军重用并完成了导弹项目开发。

• **jasonhong**的观点：提到Garwin在IBM的贡献，包括磁共振成像、触屏显示器、激光打印机等。jasonhong特别强调了Garwin在23岁时设计了第一个可用的氢弹，突显了他在核武器发展中的重要角色。

• **smartbit**的观点：指出Garwin是Pugwash会议的成员，积极参与多个国际科学会议，并与苏联科学家合作，提出限制核武库和太空武器的建议。smartbit强调了Garwin在国际科学合作和军备控制方面的贡献。

• **Supermancho**的观点：质疑冷战期间关于核武器威力的评估，特别是对一个相当于600,000个广岛原子弹威力的核武器的实际效果提出疑问。Supermancho探讨了评估中的潜在误差来源，如空气压力和爆炸效果的差异。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Hilift和jasonhong对Hall和Garwin在核武器发展中的角色持不同看法。Hilift更关注Hall的间谍活动及其政治背景，而jasonhong则强调Garwin在核武器设计和科技领域的成就。
• **合作与冲突**：smartbit补充了Garwin在军备控制和国际合作方面的努力，与Hilift和jasonhong对Garwin在核武器发展中角色的强调形成对比。
• **技术评估**：Supermancho对核武器威力的技术评估提出质疑，提供了一个关于核武器实际效果的不同视角。

总体来看，讨论围绕Garwin和Hall的个人历史、技术成就及政治影响展开，涉及他们在核武器发展和军备控制中的不同角色和贡献。

data.author: mhb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对AI领域中“护城河”（moat）的讨论，包括哪些因素能够构成持久的竞争优势。

不同观点：
• [smodo] 认为许多关于AI未来的文章过于自信且预测性强，将其比作冒险小说，暗示这些文章可能夸大了对未来的预见能力。

• [AnotherGoodName] 指出，虽然AI公司可能拥有难以复制的训练模型权重作为护城河，但若在基础设施上投入5亿美元，则类似于航空公司的高债务低利润模式，质疑这种高投入是否能形成有效的护城河。

• [djoldman] 认为模型、基础设施和应用都可能成为护城河，目前尚无定论。不同类型的护城河可能在不同层面上发挥作用。

• [gwern] 关注文章的写作风格，指出作者让ChatGPT代写文章的现象，并对其合理性提出质疑。

• [KasianFranks] 强调独特、专业、高价值且难以复制的数据和数据集将成为新的竞争优势和护城河。

• [mhb] 认为AI领域的竞争是赢家通吃，护城河的概念可能不适用。高投资是否合理取决于赢得整个市场的可能性。

• [alephnerd] 强烈反对关于AI和ML的炒作，认为这种炒作可能导致行业泡沫和崩溃，类似于2000年代的电信泡沫。还指出，开发基础模型和数据中心的成本不能构成有效的护城河。

• [VirusNewbie] 不同意“模型不能构成护城河”的观点，以Meta和Microsoft为例，指出他们尚未推出最先进的基础模型，说明模型仍可能是重要的竞争优势。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于哪些因素可以构成AI领域的有效护城河，包括模型、基础设施、应用和数据等不同方面。
• 投资与回报的关系也是一个讨论重点，特别是高额投资是否能够带来可持续的竞争优势。
• 对AI和ML领域过度炒作的担忧以及可能引发的行业问题也被提及。

data.title: The Annotated Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (Kan)
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary:
《带注释的Kolmogorov-Arnold网络（KAN）指南》介绍了KAN网络，并提供了直观的代码解释，灵感来自《带注释的Transformer》。该指南是一个功能齐全的独立笔记，旨在帮助理解KAN的结构和训练过程，代码大多易于跟随，模仿了PyTorch中的标准深度学习模型。文章分为两部分：第一部分描述了KAN的基本架构和训练循环，不涉及B样条优化；第二部分讨论了B样条优化及应用。

KAN是一种不同于传统多层感知器（MLP）的表示方法，通过重构MLP中的权重矩阵-向量乘法来参数化激活函数。尽管KAN的理论证明不如MLP完善，但它在可解释性和数据效率方面提供了新的探索方向。KAN基于Kolmogorov-Arnold表示定理，能表示连续光滑的多变量函数，通过优化损失函数来学习这些函数的参数。文章还讨论了KAN层的定义及其参数化方法。
