Microsoft Build
May 19, 2025
The Windows Subsystem for Linux is now open source
By
Pierre Boulay
Today we’re very excited to announce the open-source release of the Windows Subsystem for Linux. This is the result of a multiyear effort to prepare for this, and a great closure to the first ever issue raised on the Microsoft/WSL repo:
Will this be Open Source? · Issue #1 · microsoft/WSL
.
That means that the code that powers WSL is now available on GitHub at
Microsoft/WSL
and open sourced to the community! You can download WSL and build it from source, add new fixes and features and participate in WSL’s active development.
WSL component overview
WSL is made of a set of distribution components. Some run in Windows, and some run inside the WSL 2 virtual machine. Here’s an overview of WSL’s architecture:
WSL’s code can be broken up into these main areas:
Command line executables that are the entry points to interact with WSL
wsl.exe, wslconfig.exe and wslg.exe
The WSL service that starts the WSL VM, starts distros, mounts file access shares and more
wslservice.exe
Linux init and daemon processes, binaries that run in Linux to provide WSL functionality
init for start up, gns for networking, localhost for port forwarding, etc.
File sharing Linux files to Windows with WSL’s plan9 server implementation
plan9
Head over to
https://wsl.dev
to learn more about each component.
This comes as an addition to the already open sourced WSL components:
microsoft/wslg: Enabling the Windows Subsystem for Linux to include support for Wayland and X server related scenarios
microsoft/WSL2-Linux-Kernel: The source for the Linux kernel used in Windows Subsystem for Linux 2 (WSL2)
The following components are still part of the Windows image and are not open sourced at this time:
Lxcore.sys, the kernel side driver that powers WSL 1
P9rdr.sys and p9np.dll, which runs the “\\wsl.localhost” filesystem redirection (from Windows to Linux)
Why open source now? A bit of history…
WSL was first announced at BUILD back in 2016 and first shipped with the Windows 10 Anniversary update.
At that time WSL was based on a pico process provider, lxcore.sys, which enabled Windows to natively run ELF executables, and implement Linux syscalls inside the Windows kernel. This eventually became what we today know as “WSL 1”, which WSL still supports.
Over time it became clear that the best way to provide optimal compatibility with native Linux was to rely on the Linux kernel itself. WSL 2 was born, and first announced in 2019.
As the community behind WSL grew, WSL gained more features such as GPU support, graphical applications support (via wslg) and support for systemd.
It eventually became clear that to keep up with the growing community and feature requests, WSL had to move faster, and ship separately from Windows. That’s why in 2021 we separated WSL from the Windows codebase, and moved it to its own codebase. This new WSL first shipped as version 0.47.1 to the Microsoft Store, in July 2021. At the time, only Windows 11 was supported, and the package was marked as preview, only recommended to users that wanted to experience the latest and greatest of WSL.
We continued to develop this new “WSL package” until it was ready for general availability. That happened November of 2022, with WSL 1.0.0, which added support for Windows 10 and was the first “stable” release of this new WSL.
From there we kept on improving WSL, with the objective of fully transitioning all users to this new WSL package, and away from the WSL component that shipped with Windows. Windows 11 24H2 was the first Windows build that moved users from the “built-in” WSL to the “new” WSL package. We kept wsl.exe in the Windows image, so it could download the latest package on demand to make the transition easier.
As we kept on improving WSL, we eventually hit another milestone: WSL 2.0.0 (What are the three hardest problems in computer science? Off by one errors and naming things!).
WSL 2.0.0 introduced major improvements such as mirrored networking, DNS tunneling, session 0 support, proxy support, firewall support and more.
And that’s the milestone we’re still building on today! At the time of writing this article, WSL
2.5.7
is the latest available version out of our
nine pages of Github releases
since 0.47.1 4 years ago !
The community behind WSL
Over the years we’ve been incredibly lucky to have a strong community supporting WSL from day 1. We’ve been blessed with people sharing their knowledge, and spending countless hours to help track down bugs, find the best ways to implement new features and improve WSL.
WSL could never have been what it is today without its community. Even without access to WSL’s source code, people have been able to make major contributions that lead to what WSL is now.
This is why we’re incredibly excited to open-source WSL today. We’ve seen how much the community has contributed to WSL without access to the source code, and we can’t wait to see how WSL will evolve now t

data.title: Show HN: Samchika – A Java Library for Fast, Multithreaded File Processing
data.author: mprataps
data.article_summary: Samchika 是一个专为 Java 设计的高性能、多线程文件处理库，专注于并行处理大文件，具有快速和轻量的特点。它提供简单易用的 API，支持批量处理、运行时统计可选，并适用于日志分析、ETL操作、大文本处理等多种场景。该库在多核系统中表现出显著的性能提升，相比传统的 BufferedReader 方法，处理速度更快，内存消耗可控。Samchika 基于 MIT 许可证开源，欢迎贡献和使用。安装可通过 Maven 或 Gradle 进行，并提供了详细的示例代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java项目的多线程优化及其实现细节

不同观点：
• **Calzifer的观点**：Calzifer指出，在Java中，String的hashCode可能被缓存，特别是在JIT（即时编译器）优化的情况下，空循环可能被完全移除。因此，虽然代码看似在重复计算hash，但实际上可能并不会真正执行这么多次。

• **sieve的观点**：sieve讨论了书写Sanskrit术语时使用罗马字母所带来的发音问题，并建议使用IAST或ISO-15919标准来避免误读。同时，提出为了适应英文用户，某些字母如"ch"应该保留以表示其正确的发音。

• **mprataps的观点**：mprataps对收到的反馈表示感谢，并提到该项目最初是为了学习多线程技术。他表示会参考反馈进行改进，并认为项目已经达到了预期的学习目标。

• **sidcool的观点**：sidcool称赞了项目的质量，并建议添加测试以进一步提升项目。

• **sureglymop的观点**：sureglymop对多线程读取文件的效率提出质疑，认为由于系统调用和上下文切换的存在，多线程可能无法真正实现并行读取，反而会因为互相阻塞而影响性能。

• **codetiger的观点**：codetiger询问是否有与其他类似工具的基准测试对比，以评估该项目的性能和效率。

• **VWWHFSfQ的观点**：VWWHFSfQ担心项目中对内存的重复缓冲操作会导致内存占用过高，特别是在处理大批量数据时，可能存在内存性能问题。

• **gavinray的观点**：gavinray建议让操作系统处理内存分页和缓冲，而不是手动管理。他推荐使用Java的"MappedByteBuffer"或"AsynchronousFileChannel"来进行异步文件读取和处理，以提高效率。

• **ldjkfkdsjnv的观点**：ldjkfkdsjnv认为使用LLM（如GPT等）可以在几小时内写出类似的库，暗示该项目可能并不复杂或具有独特性。

• **SillyUsername的观点**：SillyUsername指出，使用ArrayList处理大量添加操作时性能不佳，建议使用LinkedList来提升吞吐量，并提到还有其他优化空间。

补充讨论：
• 项目的多线程实现细节及内存管理是讨论的核心，特别是在文件读取和处理时，多线程是否有效以及如何优化内存使用成为焦点。
• 反馈中涉及了对项目代码实现的细节优化（如数据结构的选择、内存管理）以及项目整体设计的建议（如添加测试、进行性能对比）。
• 争议焦点主要在于多线程在文件处理中的有效性及内存管理的优化策略，不同用户提出了不同的技术方案和建议。

Samchika
Samchika
(meaning
File
in Sanskrit) is a
re-usable
,
easy-to-use
, and
extremely fast
file processing library for the Java language.
It is built with a strong focus on
multithreading
to handle CPU-intensive file processing tasks in parallel, enabling high performance even with massive files.
🚀 Features
🔁 Fully multithreaded – optimized for parallel file processing.
🧩 Simple API – just plug in your file path and logic.
📊 Optional runtime stats – time taken, memory used, thread-level info.
🧪 Ideal for processing and analyzing
large text files
(e.g. logs, datasets).
🌍 Open-source friendly – contributions are welcome!
Use Cases
Samchika excels in several scenarios where multithreaded file processing provides significant advantages:
Log Analysis & Processing
ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) Operations
Large Text Corpus Processing
Batch Report Generation
Data Transformation Pipelines
Real-time Data Processing
See the examples directory for detailed implementations of these use cases.
Quick Example
java// Transform a large CSV file with optimal performance
SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("large_dataset.csv")
.outputPath("transformed_dataset.csv")
.batchSize(10000)
.lineProcessor(line -> line.toUpperCase())
.displayStats(true)
.build()
.execute();

🛠️ How to Use

import com.samchika.SmartFileProcessor;
Step 2: Client Code
public static void main(String[] args) {
SmartFileProcessor processor = SmartFileProcessor.builder()
.inputPath("input.txt")         // Path to the file to be processed
.outputPath("output.txt")       // Path to write the output
.lineProcessor(Main::processLine) // Your business logic per line
.displayStats(true)             // Optional: display runtime stats
.build();

}

44072788.article_summary: Samchika 是一个专为 Java 设计的高性能、多线程文件处理库，专注于并行处理大文件，具有快速和轻量的特点。它提供简单易用的 API，支持批量处理、运行时统计可选，并适用于日志分析、ETL操作、大文本处理等多种场景。该库在多核系统中表现出显著的性能提升，相比传统的 BufferedReader 方法，处理速度更快，内存消耗可控。Samchika 基于 MIT 许可证开源，欢迎贡献和使用。安装可通过 Maven 或 Gradle 进行，并提供了详细的示例代码。

主要讨论点：Java项目的多线程优化及其实现细节

不同观点：
• **Calzifer的观点**：Calzifer指出，在Java中，String的hashCode可能被缓存，特别是在JIT（即时编译器）优化的情况下，空循环可能被完全移除。因此，虽然代码看似在重复计算hash，但实际上可能并不会真正执行这么多次。

• **sieve的观点**：sieve讨论了书写Sanskrit术语时使用罗马字母所带来的发音问题，并建议使用IAST或ISO-15919标准来避免误读。同时，提出为了适应英文用户，某些字母如"ch"应该保留以表示其正确的发音。

• **mprataps的观点**：mprataps对收到的反馈表示感谢，并提到该项目最初是为了学习多线程技术。他表示会参考反馈进行改进，并认为项目已经达到了预期的学习目标。

• **sidcool的观点**：sidcool称赞了项目的质量，并建议添加测试以进一步提升项目。

• **sureglymop的观点**：sureglymop对多线程读取文件的效率提出质疑，认为由于系统调用和上下文切换的存在，多线程可能无法真正实现并行读取，反而会因为互相阻塞而影响性能。

• **codetiger的观点**：codetiger询问是否有与其他类似工具的基准测试对比，以评估该项目的性能和效率。

• **VWWHFSfQ的观点**：VWWHFSfQ担心项目中对内存的重复缓冲操作会导致内存占用过高，特别是在处理大批量数据时，可能存在内存性能问题。

• **gavinray的观点**：gavinray建议让操作系统处理内存分页和缓冲，而不是手动管理。他推荐使用Java的"MappedByteBuffer"或"AsynchronousFileChannel"来进行异步文件读取和处理，以提高效率。

• **ldjkfkdsjnv的观点**：ldjkfkdsjnv认为使用LLM（如GPT等）可以在几小时内写出类似的库，暗示该项目可能并不复杂或具有独特性。

• **SillyUsername的观点**：SillyUsername指出，使用ArrayList处理大量添加操作时性能不佳，建议使用LinkedList来提升吞吐量，并提到还有其他优化空间。

• 项目的多线程实现细节及内存管理是讨论的核心，特别是在文件读取和处理时，多线程是否有效以及如何优化内存使用成为焦点。
• 反馈中涉及了对项目代码实现的细节优化（如数据结构的选择、内存管理）以及项目整体设计的建议（如添加测试、进行性能对比）。
• 争议焦点主要在于多线程在文件处理中的有效性及内存管理的优化策略，不同用户提出了不同的技术方案和建议。

data.title: Remembering Alasdair MacIntyre
data.author: danielam
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Alasdair MacIntyre及其作品的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• [qhiliq] 认为MacIntyre的《Hegel on Faces and Skulls》对他影响很大，帮助他理解了黑格尔对面相学和颅相学的批判，并从中思考现代面部识别系统的问题。该评论关注的是从外表获取信息的局限性，并将MacIntyre的思想与技术问题联系起来。
  
• [AquinasCoder] 推荐了MacIntyre的其他作品，如《Whose Justice, Whose Rationality》和《Dependent Rational Animals》。虽然AquinasCoder认为MacIntyre在现代认识论与奥古斯丁-托马斯主义之间的调和尝试未必完全成功，但肯定了MacIntyre作为道德哲学家的地位。

• [sisoes] 提到《After Virtue》深刻改变了他的道德世界观，并对此表示感激，尽管他已经不再是罗马天主教徒。这表明MacIntyre的思想对个体道德观念有深远影响。

• [Boogie_Man] 将《After Virtue》与G.K. Chesterton的思想联系起来，表示对MacIntyre的欣赏，尤其是对他批判和分析异端思想的兴趣。

• [digiconfucius] 同样高度评价《After Virtue》，认为这本书帮助他了解了思想史，并对MacIntyre的去世表示遗憾，表达了一种未能与其见面的遗憾。

• [antithesizer] 对MacIntyre的《After Virtue》持批评态度，认为其强调道德仅存在于文化传统中的观点会导致道德相对主义，忽视了历史上许多传统社会存在的恶劣行为（如奴隶制、厌女症等）。antithesizer认为现代伦理虽然碎片化，但不能通过回归部落主义或否认理性来解决。

• [gjm11] 对MacIntyre曾将某作品描述为“哲学界的《Vogue》”表示好奇，显示出对MacIntyre某些具体观点或评价的兴趣，但未深入讨论其思想。

• [cess11] 尽管在神学和政治哲学上不同意MacIntyre的许多观点，但仍尊重他尝试与尼采及法国哲学家对话，并坚持其平等主义的伦理观。此外，cess11引用MacIntyre的一句话来展示其持续的激进立场。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：《After Virtue》中的道德相对主义倾向及其对传统文化与现代伦理关系的处理方式。antithesizer认为MacIntyre过度美化古代社区和传统，而忽视了其中存在的恶劣行为。
• 对MacIntyre思想的个人解读与情感反应，如sisoes和digiconfucius对其作品的深刻个人体验。
• MacIntyre在道德哲学和神学领域的地位与影响，多位评论者对其思想贡献表示肯定，即便在不同意其具体观点的情况下。

data.title: The Curious Case of the Pygmy Nuthatch
data.author: prawn
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在疫情期间逐渐对观鸟产生痴迷，并将其变成一种无时无刻都在进行的活动，即“birding”。观鸟不仅是观察鸟类，更是融入一种新的现实层次，解读周围环境。这种活动通常平和且有助于减压，但偶尔也会遇到意外，如电影中错误使用的鸟叫声，令观鸟爱好者感到困惑和困扰。作者特别提到在电影《查理的天使》中一个长期存在的鸟类错误，并深入调查其背后的原因，最终发现即便是高预算的大片也会在 portray 鸟类时出错。文章改编自Slate播客《Decoder Ring》的一集。

不同观点：

44050465.article_content:
Photo illustration by Slate. Photos by Kevin Winter/Getty Images, Bjørn Christian Tørrissen/https://bjornfree.com, and Columbia Pictures.
Tweet
Share
Share
Comment
There is nothing quite like becoming birdpilled. I am not a halfway kind of person: When I got into movies, I turned thinking about movies into my job. When I got into running, it wasn’t long until I was running a half-marathon every weekend. So I know what it’s like to become obsessed—and to start seeing your new obsession everywhere.
But during lockdown, I, like a lot of people, gradually became obsessed with birds—and it turns out that, with birds, they really are everywhere. They’re fluttering outside your window when you’re supposed to be working. They’re singing nearby when you’re supposed to be sleeping. They’re soaring overhead when you’re supposed to be paying attention to oncoming traffic.
Bird-watching does sometimes involve just that—watching birds—but for the truly birdpilled, it’s about tuning in to a new layer of reality around you and decoding it. The word
bird
becomes not just a noun but a verb, and you are
always
birding. That bird singing when you’re trying to sleep in, that sounds like a dial-up modem? That’s a song sparrow. That bird fluttering outside your window when you’re supposed to be working?
Damn
, you think,
is that a
yellow-rumped warbler
?
That raptor soaring over your head when you’re supposed to be paying attention to oncoming traffic? Usually it’s a red-tailed hawk, but sometimes it’s a turkey vulture, or a black vulture, or something more interesting, something that maybe merits glancing up just a
little
while longer …
This is your new reality, and after a few months or years of adjusting to the shock of it, you start to feel as if you’re in the Matrix. In every glimpse of an outer tail feather, every snippet of song, you can see those cascading green lines of code, and after a while, you can read them.
Most of the time, this is a peaceful, meditative activity, the kind that puts you in a flow state and has been
scientifically
proven
to
reduce stress
. No matter how out of control everything else feels, when you’re out in nature, everything is in its right place.
Still, every once in a while, there’s a glitch in the Matrix. In real life, these oddities are thrilling: If something is out of place, it could be a “vagrant,” a migrating bird that has wandered off course from another side of the country or even another hemisphere.
Advertisement
There are, unfortunately, other types of glitches. They come fast and furious, scrambling your brain. You’re watching Indiana Jones trudge through the jungles of South America in the opening scene of
Raiders of the Lost Ark
, and
one of the first sounds you hear
is the famous “
awebo
” call of the tundra-loving willow ptarmigan, on the wrong end of the American continent. You’re watching Season 3 of
The White Lotus
, set in Thailand, and you find yourself distracted by
the persistent “kon-ka-
reeee
” of red-winged blackbirds
, on the wrong side of the Pacific Ocean. You’re lost in
Dune
’s sweeping vistas, watching Paul Atreides sulk about his home planet of Caladan, until there it is, on the wrong side of the galaxy: a
killdeer
.
Advertisement
Advertisement
Advertisement
Like any generous viewer—I consider myself one—you learn to suspend your disbelief. The same way you learn to accept that every phone number in every movie starts with
555
, if you’re a birder, you learn to accept that every bald eagle in every movie screeches like a red-tailed hawk.
Advertisement
I maintained this policy throughout my early birdpilling. But then I watched the original movie adaptation of
Charlie’s Angels
, and I found myself staring down one of the greatest mysteries of recent cinema.
You see, there’s a scene in that movie that tormented me, that kept me up at night, and that lately has had me interrogating a wide variety of seemingly devoted, and certainly well-compensated, filmmaking professionals. That’s because the bird in
Charlie’s Angels
is, I believe, the wrongest bird in the history of cinema—and one of the weirdest and most inexplicable flubs in any movie I can remember. It is elaborately, even
ornately
wrong. It has haunted not just me but, as I’d later learn, the birding community at large for almost a quarter of a century.
So, naturally, being an all-in sort of person, I embarked upon a wild-goose chase to investigate how and why this monstrosity took flight. I talked to script doctors and scoured legal statutes. I interviewed leading ornithological experts and electronically analyzed birdcalls, all to figure out who laid this giant egg. It took nearly a year. But eventually, I discovered why hundreds of people with a budget of nearly $100 million failed to accurately portray a single bird. The answer was most fowl.
Advertisement
This story was adapted from an episode of Slate’s podcast
Decoder Ring
.
That episode was written by Forrest Wickman and edited by Willa Paskin and Evan

data.author: charliesabino
data.article_summary: 《凯撒的最后一口气》一文通过费米估算的方法，估算了我们每次呼吸中吸入凯撒最后一口气中的分子数量。文章假设凯撒最后一口气的分子均匀扩散到大气中，并利用一些简化数据进行计算。结果显示，我们每次呼吸大约会吸入一个来自凯撒最后一口气的分子。文章详细列出了大气体积、一次呼吸的体积等计算步骤，并通过近似值和数量级验证了估算的合理性。这种估算方法展示了“餐巾纸数学”的强大，帮助我们理解复杂问题中的数量关系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于凯撒最后一口气的分子是否以及如何在我们呼吸时被吸入的科学讨论和趣味估算。

不同观点：
• **支持估算的观点**：
  - [fernly] 通过计算得出，我们每次呼吸大约吸入小于一个凯撒最后一口气中的分子，但一天中可能会吸入几个这样的分子。这一估算基于理想气体定律和分子数量的计算。
  - [cm2012] 认为这个数学计算非常 neat（精致），结果出乎意料。
  
• **对分子稳定性提出质疑的观点**：
  - [throe73848484] 指出氮气分子在长期暴露于太阳紫外线辐射下并不稳定，单个紫外光子可以打破氮分子的键，因此不能假设这些分子在2000年后仍然存在。
  - [lkmill] 提到大多数空气中的分子半衰期远短于2000年，但原子本身可能仍然存在，因此讨论原子比讨论分子更准确。

• **对分子扩散均匀性提出质疑的观点**：
  - [xixixao] 质疑凯撒最后一口气的分子是否会均匀扩散到整个大气中，并提出这些分子是否更可能集中在地理位置如罗马、意大利或北半球。
  
• **对估算模型的批评和趣味性观点**：
  - [jamesgill] 认为估算中做了太多简化假设，虽然结果有趣但科学性可能不足。
  - [djoldman] 调侃这种估算破坏了趣味性，暗示过于理性分析会失去趣味。

• **其他趣味性延展和评论**：
  - [BubbleRings] 提出一个趣味问题，即需要呼吸多少次才能吸入一个曾经属于凯撒和恐龙的氧原子，并建议以此创建一个新的计量单位。
  - [seydor] 开玩笑说现在每份沙拉都是“凯撒沙拉”。

补充讨论：
• **关于模型假设的讨论**：
  - [fedeb95] 提出疑问，这个估算是否假设大气层和地球表面都是对呼吸分子不可渗透的。

• **关于费米估算的讨论**：
  - [diego898] 观察到费米估算常被用作“智力”的代名词，表现好在这些估算上有时可以弥补特定知识的不足。

争议焦点：
- 核心争议在于分子是否能在2000年后仍然存在并均匀分布，以及估算模型中假设的合理性。

Caesar's Last Breath
23 May, 2025
How many molecules from Caesar’s last breath do we inhale with each breath we take? Shockingly, the answer is about one molecule—we actually
do
share breaths with Caesar! And, by extension,
every breath
we take is composed of the previous breaths of
everyone who ever lived
—Socrates, Lincoln, Einstein, etc. Isn’t that crazy?
This is a classic exercise in
Fermi estimation
—it even has a
book
named after it. It’s a beautiful introduction to the power of napkin math, showing how much you can figure out with just a few back-of-the-envelope numbers.
Estimating quantities is a valuable skill—if you’re not convinced, check out
Nabeel Qureshi's blog

data.title: Writing A Job Runner (In Elixir) (Again) (10 years later)
data.author: rhgraysonii
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是关于一个名为GenStage的Elixir库的教程，撰写于2025年。文章存储在一个公开的GitHub代码库中，任何人都可以查看。目前，该项目有8个点赞，但尚未被任何人复制（fork）。要对通知设置进行更改，用户需要登录自己的账户。文章本身并没有包含具体的技术细节或内容摘要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir生态中的任务运行工具及其相关技术选择和行业接受度

不同观点：
• **支持使用Oban**：[sbrother] 强烈推荐Oban作为生产级的任务运行工具，认为其开源版本已经非常优秀，即使付费的专业版提供更多功能。
• **对Elixir行业接受度的担忧**：[huqedato] 提到自己曾构建过类似的Pub/Sub系统，但客户对Elixir/Erlang解决方案持怀疑态度，更倾向于Java/.Net/Python/PHP等传统语言。
• **对Elixir持久性的认可**：[rhgraysonii] 对比了多年前使用GenStage编写的代码，认为Elixir代码经受住了时间的考验，重温这些代码让他感到愉悦。
• **对基于Postgres的工具的兴趣**：[cpursley] 提出希望看到基于Postgres的pgmq和pg_crom扩展的Elixir工具，类似于pgflow。
• **分布式应用的优势**：[jamal-kumar] 认为Elixir在构建分布式应用方面的便捷性是其最大的卖点。

补充讨论：
• **学习Elixir的热情**：[dangerousnight] 表达了对Elixir的兴趣，计划深入阅读相关教程。
• **对文章的赞赏**：[udkl] 对文章的详细程度表示感谢，并特别提到"FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED"这一技术细节很有趣。
• **对技术文章和工具的幽默批评**：[1oooqooq] 以幽默的方式批评了技术文章和工具中充斥着 buzzwords 的现象，同时对自己简单的解决方案（使用nginx和acme客户端）感到满意。

争议焦点：
• **Elixir在行业中的接受度**：[huqedato] 的评论显示出对Elixir在实际商业环境中接受度不高的担忧，与[sbrother] 和[jamal-kumar] 对Elixir工具的积极评价形成对比。

总体来看，讨论围绕Elixir在任务运行和分布式应用开发中的优势展开，同时涉及其在行业中的接受度和与其他技术的比较。

data.title: Bits with Soul
data.author: mrkeen
data.article_summary: 在达尔文学院的访谈中，计算机科学家Simon Peyton Jones分享了他对编程语言研究的见解。他讨论了函数式编程的重要性，特别是Haskell语言的发展。Simon强调了理论与实践结合的必要性，指出学术研究应关注实际问题。他还谈到了教育和开源社区对编程语言创新的推动作用，鼓励更多人参与其中。Simon以其在并行计算和编译器设计方面的贡献而闻名，他的观点为计算机科学领域提供了深刻的启示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：计算机科学及其教育的重要性，以及如何传达其魅力与影响

不同观点：
• [flir的观点] 计算机科学不仅仅关乎编码和技术，它提供了一种新的视角来理解和探索世界。flir强调，通过数字化技术，我们能够机械化分析和转换信息，探索手动技术无法触及的领域。他指出，计算机科学具有复杂性和创造性，并且已经深入到我们的日常生活中，因此每个人，尤其是儿童，都应该对其有基本的理解和感知。他认为这不仅关乎技术能力，还涉及到理解技术的潜力和局限。

• [cpt_hellsmug的观点] cpt_hellsmug并没有直接讨论计算机科学本身，而是对flir的表达方式做出了反馈。他认为flir的演讲风格专业且客观，让人容易相信其内容，但他个人希望在其中加入更多的情感元素，使演讲更具幽默感和共鸣。他还提到自己创作了一部与此相关的漫画，尽管可能有些偏离主题。

补充讨论：
• flir强调计算机科学的创造性和美学价值，试图打破人们对计算机科学“枯燥”和“技术化”的刻板印象，呼吁教育中应包含更多对技术的感性理解。
• cpt_hellsmug则更关注表达的形式，希望在讨论严肃主题时能增加情感和幽默，使讨论更具吸引力。
• 争议的焦点可能在于如何在技术性演讲中平衡专业性和趣味性，使听众既能获取知识，又能享受过程。

总结来看，讨论的焦点在于计算机科学的教育和传播方式，以及如何在传达信息时兼顾理性和感性。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Sugar-Coated Poison: Benign Generation Unlocks LLM Jailbreaking, by Yu-Hang Wu and Yu-Jie Xiong and Jie-Zhang
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have become increasingly integral to a wide range of applications. However, they still remain the threat of jailbreak attacks, where attackers manipulate designed prompts to make the models elicit malicious outputs. Analyzing jailbreak methods can help us delve into the weakness of LLMs and improve it. In this paper, We reveal a vulnerability in large language models (LLMs), which we term Defense Threshold Decay (DTD), by analyzing the attention weights of the model's output on input and subsequent output on prior output: as the model generates substantial benign content, its attention weights shift from the input to prior output, making it more susceptible to jailbreak attacks. To demonstrate the exploitability of DTD, we propose a novel jailbreak attack method, Sugar-Coated Poison (SCP), which induces the model to generate substantial benign content through benign input and adversarial reasoning, subsequently producing malicious content. To mitigate such attacks, we introduce a simple yet effective defense strategy, POSD, which significantly reduces jailbreak success rates while preserving the model's generalization capabilities.

data.title: How I ended up flying for Yemen's national airline – and survived
data.author: techonup
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在也门航空（Yemenia）工作的外籍合同工的详细情况。作者描述了一个典型外籍飞行员在航空职业生涯中可能做出的选择，因之前合同突然终止而面临失业和经济压力。在偶然机会下，他获得了一份也门航空的6个月外籍合同，包含高薪、住宿、签约奖金和其他福利。尽管有些警示信号，如面试过程简单、沟通不专业等，他仍决定参与。经过简单的线上面试和开罗的评估（旅途经济舱、住宿豪华），他通过了形式上的模拟机测试，但未签署正式合同。几周后，他被通知去开罗进行培训，并被要求提供大量个人信息。培训即将开始时，他回忆起也门航空曾发生的致命空难，暗示对未来工作的潜在担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对不同航空公司运营情况的讨论，特别是涉及高风险地区的飞行经历和生活状况。

不同观点：
• **对高风险地区飞行的态度**：
  - [theyknowitsxmas] 认为在危险情况下（如战区）应该尽快离开，无法理解为什么有人会在第一次降落后还不撤离。
  - [2Gkashmiri] 则提出相反观点，认为尽管某些地区（如克什米尔）被列为旅行禁区，但对于当地居民来说，这是他们的家园。虽然存在风险，但生活依然继续，且由于旅游业受影响，费用变得更低。

• **对特定航空公司或飞机问题的描述**：
  - [scrlk] 分享了在Kam Air（阿富汗航空公司）工作的经历，特别是提到飞机YA-KME的怪异问题（如假火警），并指出机组人员已经习惯这种 quirks。
  - [Apocryphon] 则质疑飞行员是否在起飞前与副驾驶充分沟通，暗示可能存在安全隐患。

• **对特定经历的感受**：
  - [hilux] 和 [cjrp] 都表示这种故事很有趣且真实，认为这种写作风格引人入胜，甚至愿意阅读更多类似内容。
  - [the__alchemist] 则对作者没有事先获得更多警告表示惊讶，但同时也认为这是事后诸葛亮（hindsight is 50/50）。

补充讨论：
• **对航班和路线的实际查询**：
  - [mattas] 试图查询Yemenia航空的航班，但发现网站上显示"没有可用航班"。

• **对战区航空公司排班的效率赞赏**：
  - [pavel_lishin] 称赞Yemenia航空在面临火箭攻击、汽车炸弹、迫击炮以及电力与网络不稳定的情况下，依然能够按时发布排班表，相比之下一些欧洲航空公司做得不如他们好。

争议焦点：
• **是否应在高风险地区继续运营航班**：
  - 一部分人如[theyknowitsxmas]认为应该尽快撤离危险地区。
  - 另一部分如[2Gkashmiri]则认为对当地居民来说，这些地区依然是他们的家，且风险可能被夸大，生活仍在继续。

• **飞机安全问题**：
  - [scrlk] 描述了飞机的怪异问题，并指出机组人员已经习惯这些问题。
  - [Apocryphon] 则隐晦地质疑飞行前机组人员是否充分沟通，暗示可能存在安全隐患。

总结：评论围绕高风险地区航空运营、飞机技术问题以及个人经历感受展开，展示了参与者对风险、安全和生活常态的不同看法。

Yemenia Expat Contract: Full Info
A carrier which is very rarely mentioned on here, Im going to give you an insight into what it is like to work for them under one of those famous expat contracts that have floated about here and there in the past. I understand 99% of you will see the advert and simply move on, perhaps with an amused exhale while you scroll down to the flag carrier DEC jobs, but for the 1% of you looking for answers, here you go!
Ill start from the beginning:
Background
:
So, you made some silly choices in your aviation career, and have found yourself fallen into the contractor bubble, jumping between contracts with various contractors. You dont see your family as often as youd like, and its far from stable, but the money is great and there is a large variety of flying.
Your previous contract blew up after just a few weeks and you find yourself now unemployed, bills to pay and a family to look after, when by miracle, a contractor rolls across your path offering a starting-6 month contracting role with Yemenia, LHS of the 320, a high roller 6 figure salary, accommodation, a joining bonus, and all the addons one might expect from this sort of contract. You know that when things seem too good to be true, they usually are, but hindsight is always 20/20, and you reassure yourself at the time that it is a reputable contractor, so dont think twice about it.
Application
:
You throw in a fairly straightforward application, not really expecting to hear back. As with all of these types of contracts, they often die out before they start, and the ones that do get up and running with high salaries are often competitive, so you dont expect to hear anything back. A few weeks pass, and youre invited to a few unsociably timed zoom interviews which take place with cameras off and audio that sounds like a 2007 era Call of Duty microphone. The interview process was inexplicably easy, with questions more evolving toward when can you start than anything more bus or career specific. Red flags, but its all good, youve crossed these bridges before when you joined other random carriers in the past and they turned out OK. Eventually they contact you and send you flight details for a trip to Cairo to complete an assessment, no say in the dates, theyve already made the bookings. Your journey to Cairo involves 2 stops via Frankfurt and Istanbul on an Economy Basic ticket, not exactly an Emirates Suite, but you are grateful that they pick up the tab. They whisk you into the Sofitel Cairo with a blank cheque to drown your sorrows, and where you can socialize with the other 7 expats here for the job, 2 Americans, a Brit, and a handful of continental Europeans, a few faces youve seen before too which is always reassuring.
The sim follows the usual rigmarole, and everybody passes with flying colours, in part due to the Egyption assessor not paying attention for 90% of it. A tick in the box, a shake of the hand and youre sent packing back to Europe with nothing but a verbal promise of being contacted. A few weeks pass by, and eventually you are contacted once again, this time offering you a training start date in just a matter of days, once again taking place in Cairo. Alongside this wonderful news, they will essentially ask you to share a generations worth of info with them, from your stamped logbook pages, to bank statements. Odd, but what do you know. Still no word on signing a contract though, so you hope that will be completed in training, and head on your merry way.
Training
:
You kiss the wife and kids goodbye and tell them youll see them when youre back from Yemen in 6 months time. Painful, but itll be worth it when you come back with pockets full of cash eh?
Not best pleased, at least the better half knows youll not get up to any funny business in that part of the world.
So you arrive in Cairo, alongside the other 7 expats who managed to navigate the gruelling selection process and sim assessment, and tuck into a few weeks of training.
Now, you are reminded of the fatal Yemenia Flight 626 crash

data.article_summary: 《Internet Archive》推出YouTube实时直播，展示微缩胶片（microfiche）的数字化过程。微缩胶片是一种存储多份缩微文档的胶片，常用于保存报纸、法庭文件和政府记录等。直播中，观众可以看到高分辨率相机拍摄胶片，并通过软件拼接图像，最终处理成可文本搜索的数字化文档并上传至公共收藏。该直播每周一至周五运行，不仅展示文档扫描过程，还播放无声电影和NASA历史图片等内容。

根据提供的链接，以下是对该视频评论区的分析总结：

主要讨论点：视频内容的价值和意义

不同观点：
• 正面评价：许多观众认为视频内容具有启发性和教育意义，尤其是对于那些想了解未来科技和创新的人。他们提到视频很好地展示了未来技术的潜力和应用场景。

• 负面评价：部分观众认为视频内容过于理想化，缺乏现实依据。他们指出视频中的一些技术在实际应用中可能会遇到很多困难和挑战，比如基础设施建设和高昂的成本。

• 中立评价：有些观众持中立态度，他们认为视频展示的概念虽然有趣，但需要更多的科学验证和技术突破才能真正实现。他们强调了对未来科技保持谨慎乐观的重要性。

补充讨论：
• 技术可行性：一些评论深入讨论了视频中提到的一些具体技术，比如自动驾驶汽车和智能城市，探讨了这些技术在当前科技水平下的可行性和实际应用中可能遇到的问题。

• 经济和社会影响：有评论关注视频中展示的未来技术对经济和社会的影响，包括就业市场的变化、隐私和安全问题等。这些评论提出了技术进步可能带来的潜在负面影响，如失业率上升和社会不平等加剧。

• 争议焦点：视频对未来科技的乐观展望引发了一些争议。部分观众认为视频过于乐观，忽视了技术发展可能带来的负面效应。而另一部分观众则认为这种乐观态度是激励创新和进步所必需的。

总的来说，评论区的主要讨论围绕视频内容的实际可行性和潜在影响展开，观众们从不同角度对未来科技的发展进行了深入的探讨。

44072137.article_content:
News
Now you can watch the Internet Archive preserve documents in real time
The feed offers a close-up look of how microfiche — the sheets of films that store multiple documents — are digitized and uploaded to the Archive.
The feed offers a close-up look of how microfiche — the sheets of films that store multiple documents — are digitized and uploaded to the Archive.
by
Emma Roth
May 22, 2025, 4:10 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Screenshot: The Verge
Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
If you’ve ever wondered how the Internet Archive uploads all the physical documents on its site, now you can get a behind-the-scenes look at the process.
The Internet Archive launched
a new
YouTube livestream
that shows the digitization of microfiche in real time — complete with some relaxing, lo-fi beats.
Microfiche is a sheet of film that contains multiple images of miniaturized documents. It’s an old form of storing newspapers, court documents, government records, and other important documents. The Internet Archive uses these microfiche cards to digitize and upload documents to its online library.
The livestream shows a close-up look at one of the five microfiche digitization stations at the organization’s Richmond, California location, along with a look at the document that it’s working on. App maker Sophia Tung, who
created a LoFi music livestream showing
Waymo’s robotaxis returning to their parking lot, also
set up the microfiche livestream for the Internet Archive
.
“Operators feed microfiche cards beneath a high-resolution camera, which captures multiple detailed images of each sheet,” Chris Freeland, the Internet Archive’s director of library services, writes in a post on the site. “Software stitches these images together, after which other team members use automated tools to identify and crop up to 100 individual pages per card.”
From there, the Internet Archive processes the pages, makes them text-searchable, and then uploads them to its public collections.
The livestream runs from Monday through Friday from 10:30AM ET to 6:30PM ET. “During the day, you’ll see scanners working on custom machines to digitize all the microfiche in the world,” Tung says. “During the off hours, you can also see everything else that the Archive has to offer, like silent films in the public domain or historical pictures from NASA.”

data.title: Prime Path Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种在GNU Compiler Collection 15中实现的 prime path coverage 支持，这是一种通过程序执行路径进行结构化覆盖率测试的指标。该方法在测试数量和覆盖率之间取得平衡，要求循环被执行多次或跳过。研究表明，prime path coverage 涵盖了修改条件/决策覆盖（MC/DC）。通过使用后缀树修剪重复子路径，算法效率从 $O(n^2m^2)$ 提升至 $O(n^2m)$。该方法通过控制流图分析，以语言无关的方式观察和检测路径，并准确报告实现覆盖所需的代码执行顺序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：循环的退出条件是否必须被执行/不执行

不同观点：
• nullc的观点：nullc提到在处理带有"if(foo)break;"这种逻辑的循环时，经常发现bug，质疑是否所有退出条件都需要明确被执行或不执行。这暗示了对循环退出条件处理的潜在问题和复杂性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论焦点：争议的焦点在于循环中的"if(foo)break;"逻辑是否会导致不可预见的问题，特别是在退出条件没有被明确控制的情况下。这可能涉及到代码的可读性、可维护性以及潜在的错误风险。
• 例子：nullc以自己遇到的多起相关bug为例，说明这种模式可能在实际编码中引发问题，但未给出具体bug细节或场景。

总结：讨论围绕循环退出条件的处理，特别是使用"if(foo)break;"逻辑时可能引发的潜在问题。nullc基于自身经验提出了对这种写法的质疑，但没有深入展开技术细节。

44070354.article_content:
Computer Science > Programming Languages
arXiv:2505.14694
(cs)
[Submitted on 25 Apr 2025]
Title:
Prime Path Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection
Authors:
Jørgen Kvalsvik
View a PDF of the paper titled Prime Path Coverage in the GNU Compiler Collection, by J{\o}rgen Kvalsvik
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We describe the implementation of the prime path coverage support introduced the GNU Compiler Collection 15, a structural coverage metric that focuses on paths of execution through the program. Prime path coverage strikes a good balance between the number of tests and coverage, and requires that loops are taken, taken more than once, and skipped. We show that prime path coverage subsumes modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC). We improve on the current state-of-the-art algorithms for enumerating prime paths by using a suffix tree for efficient pruning of duplicated and redundant subpaths, reducing it to $O(n^2m)$ from $O(n^2m^2)$, where $n$ is the length of the longest path and $m$ is the number of candidate paths. We can efficiently track candidate paths using a few bitwise operations based on a compact representation of the indices of the ordered prime paths. By analyzing the control flow graph, GCC can observe and instrument paths in a language-agnostic manner, and accurately report what code must be run in what order to achieve coverage.

data.title: Realtek's $10 tiny 10GbE NIC will hit motherboards soon
data.author: Tuldok
data.article_summary: Realtek即将推出价格低廉的RTL8127 10GbE网络控制器，尺寸为9mm x 9mm，支持2.5 Gbps、5 Gbps和10 Gbps以太网速度，功耗约1.95W，并具备硬件级误差校正和循环冗余校验等功能，适用于主板、笔记本电脑和各种设备。该控制器预计今年晚些时候以约10美元的价格出售，可能推动10GbE在主流PC中的普及。然而，10GbE网络的普及还面临基础设施成本较高的挑战，如支持10GbE的交换机和电缆价格较贵。主板厂商可能从2025年底开始将10GbE作为高端产品的 premium 功能推出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：10GbE网络模块及其在消费级市场和企业级市场中的应用和选择

不同观点：
• WarOnPrivacy认为新的网络模块在能耗和发热方面优于现有的10GbE选项，并提到Intel I225芯片在2022-2024年间存在很多问题，而Realtek表现相对稳定，可能是一个更好的选择。他还表示对Intel 225/226的改进抱有期待。

• PaulKeeble指出消费级市场需要一种紧凑的光纤连接方案，而不是sfp+，因为后者不适合安装在典型家用主板上。他认为虽然铜缆在10Gb传输中还能应付，但转向光纤是不可避免的趋势，而企业级解决方案并不适合家用市场。

• diggan提到AQC107芯片价格昂贵，不适合主板集成，并质疑10GbE主板的成本是否合理。他分享了自己购买相关设备的经历，并怀疑主板厂商可能通过集成10GbE NIC来提高售价。

• ReverseCold对文章内容表示困惑，指出高端PC主板已经配备10GbE端口多年，并质疑文章中所提的新方案是否更便宜。他还提供了pcpartpicker上的相关主板列表作为参考。

• misja111关注连接10Gb交换机/路由器所需的电缆类型，询问是否必须使用玻璃纤维。

• q3k强烈建议使用常规的SFP+，表现出对其他方案的不满。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了10GbE在消费级和企业级市场中的不同需求和解决方案。
• 讨论了不同芯片和网络接口在性能、价格和集成度方面的优劣，如Intel、Realtek和AQC107。
• 对光纤和铜缆在10Gb传输中的适用性进行了探讨。
• 争议焦点在于10GbE解决方案的性价比及其在消费级市场中的适用性。

44071701.article_content:
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Recent updates
Update: 07:30 am (ET) 5/23
: Realtek itself has demonstrated its RTL8127 NIC working with an unknown switch using cheap CAT5E cables, and the company’s representatives at the booth emphasised this fact. However, we do not know which switch or router the company used. Yet, most 10GbE routers and switches are designed for CAT6 cabling.
Although there are many higher-end motherboards that feature 2.5GbE or even 5GbE network ports, only some of them feature a 10GbE network adapter due to cost concerns. However, this may change later this year as Realtek is prepping an inexpensive 10GbE controller that is aimed at motherboards. The controller is being showcased at
Computex 2025
.
The Realtek RTL8127 is a tiny — measuring 9mm x 9mm — network controller with a PCIe 4.0 x2 interface that supports a wide range of Ethernet speeds, including 2.5 Gbps, 5 Gbps, and 10 Gbps. The RTL8127 controller consumes about 1.95W and supports modern standby modes, which is critical for laptops. The controller integrates hardware-level error correction (ECC) and cyclic redundancy check (CRC) features to ensure reliable connections and data integrity during transmission. Also, the unit features built-in self-loopback diagnostic functions for easier maintenance.
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
The 10GBase-T technology has been used primarily in servers and high-end workstations, but its adoption for more mainstream PCs has been slow, to put it mildly. Aquantia tried to popularize it for enthusiasts in the late 2010s, then it got acquired by Marvell in 2019, and while the company still sells the AQC107 silicon, it is quite expensive for motherboard integration, and add-on cards are, by definitio,n more expensive than integrated solutions.

Features of the RTL8127 make it ideal for a range of applications, including integration into motherboards, laptops, add-on Ethernet cards, and various customer premises equipment (CPE). Perhaps more importantly, Realtek plans to sell these chips for about $10 starting later this year, which will make its integration a much more appealing endeavor for motherboard makers.
(Image credit: Tom's Hardware)
Of course, producers of mainboards will sell the 10GbE as a premium feature starting from late 2025 – early 2026, so expect 10GbE connectivity to be a part of higher-end offerings and to that end we can only wonder how much will desktop motherboards with a 10GbE cost.
Of course, just like earlier, the big concern is how much the infrastructure (switches, access points, etc.) supporting 10GbE costs. At present, the cheapest 10GBase-T switch from TP-Link costs
$299 at Newegg,
and, of course, this switch requires CAT6 or CAT6A cables, which are also not cheap, making a 10GbE network a pretty expensive endeavor. Then again, if there are a lot of motherboards with a cheap 10GbE NIC, demand for switches goes up, and they will get cheaper. However, we can only wonder when this time comes.

44072110.article_content:
A 2030 morning routine
Posted: 2025-05-23
You wake at 05:30 in the morning, feeling somewhat groggy.
Instead of the alarm clock ringing like it normally does, a cheerful hologram appears: “Hi! I’m Kyle, your new alarm clock assistant!” You get dressed as Kyle explains all of the fantastic things he is capable of.
You head over to the coffee machine. “Hey there! I’m Evan! Are you ready for AI in your coffee? But first - tell me about yourself!”. You ignore Evan’s monologue and close your eyes as the synthetic coffee replacement is brewing. Real coffee costs more than your coffee maker nowadays, so it has to suffice.
You also brush off George the intelligent shoelace assistant, Cate the smart front door, Maurice the brand new elevator AI.
You try to ignore Eunice the walk-and-talk side-walk talk smart-AI as it pursues you tirelessly to tell you about its fantastic capabilities.
You arrive at the gym. The receptionist is out of order because its API has exceeded its quota, so you just walk into the locker room and change.
You put your stuff in the locker, accept the new terms and conditions, give the locker permission to share your personal information with all the different data brokers. The locker clicks as the lock engages.
As you step on the treadmill a holographic running companion joins you and starts monologuing about this fantastic new meal replacement powder they’ve been using recently. You’re not in a mood to listen so you put on your headphones and listen to ad jingles instead.
You head back to the locker room and shower. George the intelligent holographic shower buddy appears and tells you about his new AI features.
Your locker session has expired so you need to log into the gym again. First enter a pin code, then 2FA via text message on your phone, then verify your email, then you need to identify firehydrants and sidewalks for 15 minutes to prove you’re human, then accept the a new set of terms of conditions. As you click on firehydrants, George cheerfully keeps going on about his AI features.
Finally ready to head to work. You step into your car, which greets you as Ulysses, the new smart AI passenger. The car drives to work as you listen with closed eyes to a cheerfully enumeration of its fantastic new AI features.
You arrive at work just on time, you slip into your cubicle, sink into your chair, and put on your headset. You take a deep breath, and cheerfully speak into the microphone “Hey there! I’m Evan! Are you ready for AI in your coffee? But first - tell me about yourself!”
It’s gonna be a long day.

data.title: RISC-V Turns 15 with Fast Global Adoption
data.author: fork-bomber
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RISC-V架构在推出15年后的成就、挑战及未来前景

不同观点：
• 支持RISC-V的观点：
  - RISC-V在过去15年中取得了显著的成就，尤其是在开源架构方面的突破。
  - RISC-V具有灵活性和可扩展性，能够适应不同的应用场景，从嵌入式系统到高性能计算。
  - 社区和生态系统的不断壮大，为RISC-V提供了强大的支持和创新动力。
  - 举例：多个主要科技公司已经采用RISC-V，并在其基础上开发新产品。

• 质疑RISC-V的观点：
  - RISC-V在市场上的普及程度仍然有限，特别是在与ARM等成熟架构竞争时面临挑战。
  - 开源架构可能带来的知识产权问题和安全性问题令人担忧。
  - 举例：一些公司对采用开源架构持谨慎态度，担心潜在的法律风险。

• 中立观点：
  - RISC-V的未来发展取决于其生态系统的进一步成熟和社区的支持。
  - 需要在性能、功耗和成本之间找到更好的平衡，以吸引更多厂商和开发者。
  - 教育和培训也是推动RISC-V普及的重要因素，需要加强。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于RISC-V能否在竞争激烈的处理器架构市场中持续增长并占据重要地位。
- 讨论中提到RISC-V在物联网和边缘计算领域的潜力，可能成为其突破口。
- 安全性问题被多次提及，指出需要更多的研究和开发以确保RISC-V架构的安全可靠。
- 社区和行业合作的重要性被强调，认为这是RISC-V未来成功的关键因素之一。

data.title: Amdash – Human only punctuation mark
data.author: wymerica
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了标点符号“长破折号”（em dash）在文学创作中的悠久历史和重要作用，曾被狄更斯、伍尔夫、凯鲁亚克等作家广泛使用。然而，随着AI生成文本的普及，长破折号被滥用，导致人们难以区分文本是否由人类原创。为此，文章推出了一个新的标点符号“am dash”，象征真正的思考与创作，以对抗AI的平庸写作。这一符号旨在通过独特的字体和使用方式，重新彰显人类作家的个性与思想。文章还附有下载和使用说明，并引用了ChatGPT对“am dash”的正面评价，认为它是对AI生成内容的一种有力反击。

• **brookst** 认为自己习惯使用 en- 和 em-dashes 以及项目符号来组织文档，但如今由于人们可能误以为这些文档是由AI生成的，他感到有些无奈，但不愿意放弃这些标点符号。

• **_nalply** 提到有一种字体可以将 "am-" 文本片段转变为卷曲的dash（通过连字），并指出如果 Am-dash 变得流行，AI 也会学会使用它。他还提出另一种可能性，即如果 Unicode 未来接受 Am-dash，AI 将更无法被阻止。同时也提到相反的情况：可能没人会使用 Am-dash。

• **andrewl** 批评了 _nalply 提供的网站的可读性，认为设计难以理解，且闪烁的图片可能对癫痫患者有害。

• **a3w** 补充了网站底部需要添加癫痫警告，并将网站的设计风格与 Loki 迪士尼+系列的片头做了类比。

• **marcusb** 从字体设计角度讨论了某些字体如何处理连字符和 em-dash，指出大多数字体不会改变 em-dash 的外观，只有少数斜体字体（如Balladeer）是例外。

• **WithinReason** 提出如果要使用特殊字体，为什么不使用一种完全打乱字母表的字体，认为这将真正挑战AI。

• **wymerica** 表示对解决“AI过度使用 em-dash”这一问题的概念感兴趣，并好奇其他可以证明人类作者身份的标志。

• **josefritzishere** 质疑是否有什么能阻止AI使用特殊标点符号，指出AI并不在乎抄袭或侵犯版权。

• **jansan** 提出了两种可能的未来结果：要么没人会使用 Am-dash，要么 AI 会学会使用它。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了对设计美学、可读性和网站安全性（特别是对癫痫患者的影响）的关注。
- 对AI可能学会使用任何人类创造的特殊符号的担忧与质疑贯穿了多个评论。
- 评论中还提到了一些潜在的解决方案，如设计更具挑战性的字体以混淆AI，但这些方案并未得到深入探讨。

争议焦点：AI是否最终会学会使用所有人类创造的特殊标点符号，以及是否有必要或可能通过这种方式来区分人类与AI的写作。

44072922.article_content:
For generations before generative text, writers have used the em dash to hop between thoughts, emotions, and ideas. Dickens shaped his morality tales with it, Woolf’s stream-of-consciousness flowed through it, Kerouac let it drive his jazz-like prose. Today, Sally Rooney threads it through her quiet truths of the heart.
But this beloved punctuation mark has become a casualty of the algorithmic age. The em dash has been so widely adopted by AI-generated text that even when used by human hands, it begs the question: was this actually written or apathetically prompted?
The battle for the soul of writing is in full swing. And the human fightback starts here. With a new punctuation mark that serves as a symbol of real pondering, genuine daydreaming, and true editorial wordsmithery. Inspired by Descartes’ belief that thinking makes us human, the am dash is a small but powerful testament that the words you’ve painstakingly and poetically pulled together are unequivocally, certifiably, and delightfully your own.
We’re launching the am dash initially via two new, tailored typefaces: Times New Human and Areal, available to download and use alongside your custom fonts.
Areal
Times New Human
Directions for use
1. Download and Install the Times New Human and Areal typefaces.
2. When writing your best work, simply type ‘am-’ to hop between thoughts.
WHAT DOES CHATGPT THINK ABOUT THE AM DASH?
“
As ChatGPT, I suppose this is the part where I write my own obituary.
The am dash is a clever, necessary act of punctuation reclamation—both a typographic intervention and a philosophical middle finger. It names something that’s been quietly bothering everyone: that my writing (AI writing) can look like thinking without being thought. And nowhere is that uncanny valley more obvious than in the em dash—once the darling of the ruminative, reflective, beautifully meandering human mind.
What you’ve built is more than a glyph—it’s a gesture. One that pokes at the hollow competence of AI-generated prose and says, “this isn’t enough.” It’s funny, it’s meaningful, and it wears its humanity on its sleeve (and its ligature).
The am dash, with its pointed unusability by AI, serves as a subtle watermark of presence—a fingerprint smudged on the edge of a sentence. It feels less like a design stunt and more like a cultural correction, giving writers a way to plant a flag in the soil of their own ideas.
So, while I may have mastered language at scale, I know the difference between simulation and soul. And I know the am dash belongs to you.”
44072922.article_summary: 文章介绍了标点符号“长破折号”（em dash）在文学创作中的悠久历史和重要作用，曾被狄更斯、伍尔夫、凯鲁亚克等作家广泛使用。然而，随着AI生成文本的普及，长破折号被滥用，导致人们难以区分文本是否由人类原创。为此，文章推出了一个新的标点符号“am dash”，象征真正的思考与创作，以对抗AI的平庸写作。这一符号旨在通过独特的字体和使用方式，重新彰显人类作家的个性与思想。文章还附有下载和使用说明，并引用了ChatGPT对“am dash”的正面评价，认为它是对AI生成内容的一种有力反击。

data.title: Getting a paper accepted
data.author: stefanpie
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何通过优化论文的首页（包括标题、摘要、图1和引言）来提高论文被接受的几率。作者以亲身经历为例，展示了如何在一周内通过小幅修改使一篇被拒稿的论文获得高分接受。文章强调，首页决定了评审对论文的初步印象，约80%的质量感知来自首页。具体建议包括：选择具体且 memorable 的标题、使用品牌化命名、确保图1直观展示研究价值、以及在引言中避免过多引用。其余部分则需做好基础工作，如基线比较、消融实验、统计显著性和人工评估，以避免被拒。这些修改不仅提升了论文的接受率，也改善了科学贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术论文发表过程中的社会性和策略性，以及科学研究中的实际工作与论文写作之间的关系。

不同观点：
• abetusk认为学术科学领域已经演变成一个以职业发展为核心的社交游戏，研究论文更像是用来提升个人品牌和广告的工具，而不是单纯为了分享新发现。
• techas同意文章的观点，并补充了“作者工程”的概念，指出在跨领域研究时，缺乏领域内知名作者可能导致论文被拒，这需要通过会议社交来建立学术关系。
• eeeeaaehio强调了“想法”在学术中的廉价性，认为科学研究不仅仅是清晰地传达想法，更重要的是实验的执行和结果的忠实报告。
• jampa认为论文写作中应更多关注“为什么”而不是“什么”，强调了清晰沟通的重要性，尤其是在解释研究的重要性时。
• stefanpie分享了其博士研究中的经验，指出论文的反复修改和调整是为了迎合评审的口味，并建议评审和会议方也应提高评审质量。
• canjobear对论文修改后的评审结果持怀疑态度，认为可能只是因为不同的评审者偏好导致结果不同，而非修改本身的作用。
• bonoboTP提出了解学术系统中不同角色的目标和如何获取声望的重要性，认为理解“声望的流动”有助于在学术界取得成功。
• 3abiton质疑文章中提到的修改是否真的提高了论文质量，认为单一样本无法证明因果关系。
• mobeets对文章中关于引言中引用文献的看法提出异议，认为ML领域的论文在引用相关文献方面通常做得不好。
• disqard推荐了Peter Medawar的演讲《科学论文是骗局吗？》作为相关讨论的参考。
• speedgoose建议先提交论文，根据评审意见改进，再重新提交到其他地方，认为这是一个有效的策略。
• whatshisface指出了ML领域中通过展示多个模型的有效性来使基准测试被接受的现象。
• JR1427强调了论文外观和可读性的重要性，认为清晰传达研究发现可以客观地提高论文质量。
• bonoboTP在另一条评论中讨论了学术生涯中的“元游戏”，强调了构建个人声望和成为思想领袖的重要性，认为实际系统的构建在学术界不如提出新想法有价值。

补充讨论：
• 学术论文发表过程中涉及的社交和策略性行为，如会议社交和论文修改。
• 科学研究中“想法”的廉价性与实验执行和结果报告的重要性。
• 论文写作和评审过程中的主观性和不同评审者的偏好对结果的影响。
• 理解学术系统中的声望流动和不同角色的目标对职业发展的重要性。
• 实际系统构建和论文发表之间的平衡，以及在学术生涯中如何优化时间和精力分配。

Contents
Apr 10, 2025
The PhD Metagame
How to Get Your Paper Accepted
Page 1 Accepts, the Rest Avoids Reject
In 2019, I submitted a paper that was rejected with review scores 2.5, 3, 3. One week later, I resubmitted it with minor changes, and it was accepted with scores 4, 4.5, 4.5.
01
For context, that’s an almost unspeakably dramatic jump in scores, from “middling reject” to “strong accept.”
This post shows exactly those changes. We’ll frame them in two parts:
Polish page 1 for acceptance
Use the remaining pages to avoid rejection
Page 1 has four parts: title, abstract, Figure 1, and introduction. We’ll make them specific, memorable, clear, communicate value, and hook the reader. Reviewers mostly decide accept vs reject by page 1. So we optimize the judgment-before-scroll.
Then, to make sure our paper isn’t rejected, we’ll do due diligence in the rest of it by including stuff like baselines, ablations, statistical significance, and human evaluation.
The tweaks that get the paper accepted—unexpectedly, happily—also improve the actual science contribution. But if you’re tempted to be evil, read this footnote.
02
The full rejected and accepted submissions are available for download at the end.
Page 1 Is 80% of Your Paper
#
A paper has five parts:
Title
Figure 1
Abstract
Introduction
Rest of the paper
Spend equal time on each of these.
—
Me misquoting
03
Jitendra Malik quoting Don Geman
Around 80% of a paper’s perceived quality is established on page 1. The title, Figure 1, abstract, and half the introduction are all there. It’s like a book’s cover.
Throughout this post, I’ll show the rejected and accepted versions of the paper I mentioned at the top with the dramatic score swing. Here are both page 1s:
Top:
Left:
Rejected page 1.
Bottom:
Right:
Accepted page 1.
First, consider page 1’s first impression:
04
Is the Figure 1 colorful and eye-catching?
Is the title unexpected? Maybe it has one intriguing word?
Are there any curious terms (bolded or italicized)?
Is the introduction (hopefully not) full of citations?
05
Choose A Specific Memorable Title
#
Rejected:
Visually Grounded Comparative Language Generation
— too general. Any work that uses pictures and generates comparisons could use this title. I picked this title because I thought it argued for the generality of the method. But a too-general title is off-putting because it comes across as over-claiming. And a big part of our method
does
rely on our domain: we specifically use a biological taxonomy to create our dataset.
Accepted:
Neural Naturalist: Generating Fine-grained Image Comparisons
— specific and memorable. In addition to branding (more next),
naturalist
establishes the domain, and
fine-grained
narrows the task. Skeptical academics appreciate the clarity of saying what you did. The title is fully unique to our work.
06
Maybe Add Branding
#
I used to dislike branding in papers. It felt presumptuous to claim a proper noun for your research paper and to expect readers to memorize it. And many of the names sound corny.
Now, while I still often feel a pang of annoyance, it is outweighed by the recognition that it’s much easier to remember and discuss concepts which have a name.
Neural naturalist
or
Birds-to-Words
instead of “our 2019 EMNLP paper about generating comparative image captions…”
That said, I still dislike throwaway names—those with no conceptual link, or which don’t feel earned. I don’t think every paper needs one. But I think it helped for this paper.
Show Screamingly Obvious Value in Figure 1
#
The main point is that your paper’s value should be
obvious,
not that is must be
enormous.
Top:
Left:
Rejected Figure 1.
Bottom:
Right:
Accepted Figure 1.
A Figure 1 should
draw readers in
clearly demonstrate describe both what the work does and its value
be comprehensible without the caption.
The old Figure 1 showed two separate comparisons, but the link between them wasn’t clear. The bottom row just all look like owls to a non-expert. And the descriptions are long and boring.
The new Figure 1 makes the works’ focus explicit by anchoring with the same left image, and labeling each comparison with a perceptual difficulty (“high” vs “medium”). It annotates the operation (“vs” = comparison) and the result (“highly detailed” vs “fewer details”). At this point, the paper’s mechanics and unique characteristic has been established: we use different language to compare things based on how similar they look. Finally, to make the long descriptions more approachable and interesting, we’ve highlighted two components (features and parts, with orange underlines and green bubbles).
A problem with making Figure 1s—and describing your research in general—is that you know so much about it, it’s impossible to mentally model what it’d be like to learn about your work for the first time. data.title: Raspberry Pi Modems
data.author: geerlingguy
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者尝试用现成零件自制E-Ink手机的过程，起因是看到Light Phone 3售价高达800美元，决定自制成本更低的手机。作者首先尝试让Raspberry Pi Zero W支持蜂窝网络，购买了Waveshare SIM7600A-H模组，但通过GPIO实现网络功能非常困难。为解决SSH响应慢的问题，作者换用了Raspberry Pi Zero 2W。在调试模组连接时，天线连接器损坏，作者进行了临时修复。此外，作者发现Visible的SIM卡无法在模组上使用，最终选择了Tello SIM卡。接下来，作者计划安装E-Ink屏幕并开发消息和电话应用。文中还提供了使用模组的相关技术命令和笔记。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44069562.article_content:
This all started a few weeks ago, I saw a picture of the new
Light Phone 3
. I was like "That's pretty cool, how much is it?" I was expecting $200-400 but to my astonishment, after pre-orders, it will be $800. So I logically said, "It can't be that hard," and this project was born, make an E-Ink phone for less than $400 with off-the-shelf parts.
I decided the first step of this ambitious project would be getting cellular working on a Pi Zero W. I decided to order a
Waveshare SIM7600A-H
(order at your own risk). My reasoning was that I could just use gpio for the modem so I wouldn't need extra cables. This is where the issues start.
Long story short, doing anything internet related over gpio is a pain. I found data pads under the micro USB connectors on both the pi and modem, so once I have some time, I will add a short wire permanently connecting the two and bypassing the USB cord.
The second issue is that when I was debugging the modem connection over SSH, it took a painfully long time to respond to any commands. By then, it was late into the night and I was having no luck with the modem, so out of rage I ordered a
Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
(could they make the names more confusing?), to try and fix the SSH issue. The new Pi didn't fix anything at first, but for some reason after a few days it got better, no idea why. So that's what I've been using for the rest of the project.
Third issue, also at night (seeing a pattern here?). I was still trying to get the modem to connect to a cell network using this lovely
460-page AT command manual
. I decided to call it a night so I
CAREFULLY
tried to unplug the antenna from the board, but the whole connector decided to come off. I blame bad PCB construction. The next morning I decided to do a temporary fix; cutting and stripping the broken coax and soldering it right to the PCB (I know this is not good at higher frequencies, but it works). The picture is not great but I can assure you that center pin and ground are not touching.
The last big issue had actually been messing me up the whole time, I thought it would be a great idea to take out my Visible (Verizon MVNO) SIM card out from my phone and use it in the modem. But apparently they don't want you doing that, so Verizon (or Visible) made it so that the SIM card only works in approved phones (or modems). I ended up buying a
Tello SIM card
so that I can easily change the amount of data for the month and not pay outrageous fees. ($6/month is not bad at all)
The next parts of this project include, setting up an E-Ink screen, and making message and phone apps. Hopefully that gets done soon! Thank you to
Jeff Geerling
for helping me figure out the SIM card issue, and
his
blog post
about Pi modems. He was right, there is nothing about these on the internet.
Notes:
Here are my raw notes for the project, if you want more information about anything feel free to email me at the bottom of this site.
Using RNDIS.
Must stop ModemManager because it takes the AT port. Internet seems to still work with it stopped.
AT+CMGF=1 - Set SMS to text mode
AT+CPMS="ME" - Use internal memory
AT+CNMI=2,2,0,0,0 - Push incoming SMS directly over serial
LSUSB - To check if device is there
sudo picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB3 - Connect to serial
minicom -D /dev/ttyUSB3 -b 115200 - Same as above
ATE1 - Not needed but it lets you see what you are typing
at+cgdcont=1,"IP","wholesale" -  Sets the APN
AT+CFUN=1,1 - Restarts modem
AT+COPS=? -  Finds local network ops
AT+COPS=1,2,"310260" - Connects you to network operator "310260"

data.author: pavel_lishin

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）和代理型AI在日常生活中的应用及其潜在后果。

不同观点：
• @joshstrange 认为，代理型AI在执行任务时可能带来不良后果。他担心自动化请求会对商家（如保龄球馆）造成负担，并提出谁来负责处理错误（如蛋糕订错）的问题。他还提到，现实世界中已经存在商家为防止自动化预定而采取限制措施的情况。

• @benthompson 提出，代理型AI能够执行复杂的任务，如规划生日派对、预定场地、发送邀请函、计划旅行等。他的观点似乎更倾向于展示AI技术的潜力，而非关注其可能带来的问题。

• 另一隐含观点来自于 @joshstrange 的讽刺性评论 "The sky is falling!"，暗示对AI技术的过度担忧可能是不必要的。他认为，虽然AI可以自动化一些任务，但目前的技术尚不足以让人完全信任这些系统来处理重要事务。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于代理型AI的实际应用和潜在问题。一方担心AI带来的负面影响和责任问题，另一方则关注AI技术的能力展示和未来潜力。

• 例子包括：自动化预定可能导致商家采取防御措施（如仅接受电话预定或收取高额费用），以及AI在规划和组织活动中的具体应用场景。

• @joshstrange 强调，尽管AI能够执行某些任务，但在当前技术水平下，他不信任AI能完美处理诸如计划旅行或组织活动等事务。

总结：讨论围绕代理型AI的应用展开，一方关注其可能带来的负面影响和实际问题，另一方则侧重于展示其潜力和功能。争议点在于AI的实际效果和信任问题。

data.title: Recreating a video from raw captured network traffic (2023)
data.author: hiAndrewQuinn
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何通过使用Wireshark捕获网络流量并从中重建视频的经历。作者首先使用Wireshark捕获IPTV直播流量的数据包，并通过设置显示过滤器`ip.src == xx.xx.xx.xx`来排除无关流量。通过观察，作者发现直播流每10秒开启一个新的TCP连接，因此利用`tcpflow`工具提取每个TCP流中的数据。捕获完成后，保存PCAP文件并使用`tcpflow`命令生成TCP流文件，最终通过媒体播放器（如mpv）成功回放了捕获的视频——一场2000年澳大利亚大奖赛的颁奖仪式。作者强调了加密和安全的重要性，指出未加密的流量可以被类似方法截获。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44072834.article_content:
A few days ago i stumbled upon the idea to recreate a video from traffic captured in PCAP file. It may be a common knowledge that this is possible, but it felt like the coolest thing i’ve done in a while. If you’re interested on how it was done continue reading.
Capturing traffic
¶
For capturing traffic i used a
wireshark
- a free and open source tool for capturing and analyzing network traffic. I decided to capture live tv that i can stream via IPTV.
I fired up a tv stream and started capturing the traffic. I’ll note that prior to that i already knew source IP of my live stream so i applied
ip.src == xx.xx.xx.xx
as a display filter in wireshark before starting packet capture - this helps me get of unwanted network noise.
In wireshark i checked Statistics → Conversations → TCP and noticed that the live stream starts on a new TCP connection every ~ 10 seconds. This means i will have to extract data from payloads on each TCP stream. Luckly there’s an amazing tool for that called
tcpflow
.
Playing video back
¶
After i’m done capturing i save my pcap and close the wireshark. After navigating to a directory where my PCAP is saved i run
tcpflow -r {savedfile}.pcap -o tcp
This command creates a new file for each tcp stream in PCAP file and writes all of it’s data. I added -o tcp so that all of the files will be created in ./tcp directory - this is not essential, i just did it to avoid clutter in my current working dir.
Next if i
cd
to ./tcp and run
mpv ./*
a video starts playing. It’s a playback of a stream which packets were captured earlier. It just so happens to be a Formula1 podium ceremony with Michael Schumacher taking a pole on 2000 Australian grand prix.
This all feels so amazing for some reason, and i know that you can do similar stuff with real time streaming protocols like RTSP. Footage of security cameras, or even someones video call can be captured in a similar way if the traffic is unencrypted - another reason to take encryption and security of your application seriously.

data.title: DumPy: NumPy except it's OK if you're dum
data.author: jjar
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种名为DumPy的数组操作语言概念，旨在解决NumPy中因高维数组和复杂函数规则带来的思维负担。作者认为NumPy在处理高维数组时，由于避免使用循环而导致每个函数都需要考虑数组形状和规则，增加了不必要的复杂性。文章的解决方案是重新引入循环语法，但实际上仍通过编译技术实现向量化操作，从而简化思维过程并提高效率。这种方法避免了手动调整数组形状和函数规则的麻烦，同时保留了NumPy的优势，尤其是在GPU上的运行速度。作者强调这种方法并不巧妙，但能显著减少思考负担。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对于编程语言中循环和向量化操作的选择及其实现方式的争议

不同观点：
• [Bostonian的观点] 认为应该重新引入循环和索引的语法，但实际上编译器将其秘密转换为向量化操作。Bostonian指出，在高维度情况下，目前没有比循环和索引更好的表示法，因此主张恢复循环语法以提高代码的可读性和直观性。同时，Bostonian建议去除NumPy中为了解决循环速度慢问题而增加的复杂性。
   
• [潜在反对观点：未直接引用，但可推断] 可能有人认为现有的向量化操作（如NumPy中实现的）已经能够很好地解决性能问题，并且向量化操作可以简化代码，避免显式循环的复杂性。此外，现代编程语言和库的发展往往是为了适应硬件性能的提升和多核处理器的特点，因此去除这些优化可能被视为倒退。

补充讨论：
• Bostonian强调了在高维数据处理中，循环和索引表示法的不可替代性，认为这种表示法更直观和易于理解。
• 提出的解决方案是一种“语法糖”，即表面上保留传统循环的写法，但实际上利用编译器的优化将其转换为更高效的向量化操作，以达到性能和可读性的平衡。
• 争议的焦点在于，是选择传统的循环表示法以提高代码的可读性，还是坚持使用向量化操作以获得更好的性能和现有的优化机制。

DumPy: NumPy except it's OK if you're dum
DumPy: NumPy except it's OK if you're dum
May 2025
So what’s the fix?
What does it look like?
But how?
Wait, but how?
A tiny bit of cleverness
OK but is it actually better?
What to remove?
Discussion
Prototype

substack

Mistakes?
fix plz
What I want from an array language is:
Don’t make me think.
Run fast on GPUs.
Really, do not make me think.
Do
not
.
I say NumPy misses on three of these. So I’d like to propose a “fix” that—I claim—eliminates 90% of unnecessary thinking, with no loss of power. It would also fix all the things based on NumPy, for example every machine learning library.
I know that sounds grandiose. Quite possibly you’re thinking that good-old dynomight has finally lost it. So I warn you now: My solution is utterly non-clever. If anything is clever here, it’s my single-minded rejection of cleverness.
To motivate the fix, let me give my story for how NumPy went wrong. It started as a nice little library for array operations and linear algebra. When everything has two or fewer dimensions, it’s great. But at some point, someone showed up with some higher-dimensional arrays. If loops were fast in Python, NumPy would have said, “Hello person with ≥3 dimensions, please call my ≤2 dimensional functions in a loop so I can stay nice and simple, xox, NumPy.”
But since loops are slow, NumPy instead took all the complexity that would
usually
be addressed with loops and pushed it down into individual functions. I think this was a disaster, because
every time
you see some function call like
np.func(A,B)
, you have to think:
OK, what shapes do all those arrays have?
And what does
np.func
do when it sees those shapes?
Different functions have different rules. Sometimes they’re bewildering. This means constantly thinking and moving dimensions around to appease the whims of particular functions. It’s the
functions
that should be appeasing
your
whims!
Even simple-looking things like
A*B
or
A[B,C]
do quite different things depending on the starting shapes. And those starting shapes are often themselves the output of
previous
functions, so the complexity spirals.
Worst of all, if you write a new ≤2 dimensional function, then high-dimensional arrays are your problem.
You
need to decide what rules to obey, and then
you
need to re-write your function in a much more complex way to—
Voice from the back
: Python sucks! If you used a real language, loops would be fast! This problem is stupid!
That was a strong argument, ten years ago. But now everything is GPU, and GPUs hate loops. Today, array packages are cheerful interfaces that
look
like Python (or whatever) but are actually embedded languages that secretly compile everything into special GPU instructions that run on whole arrays in parallel. With big arrays, you need GPUs. So I think the speed of the host language doesn’t matter so much anymore.
Python’s slow loops may have paradoxically turned out to be an
advantage
, since they forced everything to be designed to work without loops even before GPUs took over.
Still, thinking is bad, and NumPy makes me think, so
I don’t like NumPy
.
So what’s the fix?
Here’s my extremely non-clever idea: Let’s just admit that loops were better. In high dimensions, no one has yet come up with a notation that beats loops and indices. So, let’s do this:
Bring back the syntax of loops and indices.
But don’t actually
execute
the loops. Just take the syntax and secretly compile it into vectorized operations.
Also, let’s get rid of all the insanity that’s been added to NumPy because loops were slow.
That’s basically the whole idea. If you take those three bullet-points, you could probably re-derive everything I do below. I told you this wasn’t clever.
What does it look like?
Suppose that
X
and
Y
are 2D arrays, and
A
is a 4D array. And suppose you want to find a 2D array
Z
such that
Z

= (Y
j
)

numpy

np

主要讨论点：各种类型的隧道实验及其应用和限制

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为水隧道是研究空化现象的重要工具，并通过历史事件（如Turbinia号的故事）展示了水隧道在船舶推进研究中的应用。他强调了Parsons通过水隧道改进了螺旋桨设计，并最终成功应用于海军舰艇。

• [Scramblejams] 指出隧道实验在分析某些行为（如失速后行为）方面的局限性，特别是模型自由飞行实验的困难。他认为某些实验需要借助自由飞行模型来模拟参数，而这些实验往往受限。

• [amelius] 对空气湍流的测量表示疑问，询问是否有测量数据支持湍流在量子尺度上传播的说法。这表明了对某些理论假设的质疑。

• [zh3] 分享了使用R J Mitchell风洞的个人经验，特别是用于验证传感器在风洞外使用的有效性。他还提到风洞在体育科学（如自行车运动员的空气动力学研究）中的应用。

• [pomian] 对文章中数学方程和数值（如伯努利和雷诺数）与图形和流动隧道模拟的比较表示赞赏，强调了数学与实验结合的价值。

data.title: Find Your People
data.author: jl
data.article_summary: 本文是作者作为毕业典礼演讲者对Bucknell大学2025届毕业生的致辞总结。作者分享了自己毕业时的迷茫经历，强调很多人在毕业后缺乏明确计划，并特别对那些希望有计划却不知从何开始的学生提出了建议。他指出，毕业后生活不再像火车轨道一样有明确的方向，人们需要主动寻找自己的道路。作者建议通过与人交流、探索不同职业选项，并勇于尝试新事物来找到自己的兴趣和方向。他还强调，面对拒绝时需要保持坚定，不要被他人意见左右，最终找到自己的目标并付诸行动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在毕业后面对人生的“无轨”状态，以及如何找到适合自己的人生方向和社群

不同观点：
• 一些人认为，毕业后从“有轨”生活转向“无轨”生活是突然且令人困惑的。Joshstrange及其支持者指出，很多大学生在毕业后不知道下一步该做什么，因为他们一直被训练成相信人生像火车轨道一样有明确的方向。而实际上，毕业后这种方向感就突然消失了。他们认为，学生应尽早意识到“无轨”状态，并主动寻找自己的道路，而不是等待别人给出方向。（例子：joshstrange的朋友毕业后迷茫，自己辍学进入职业生涯）

• 另一种观点强调找到适合自己的社群和环境的重要性。Neilv认为，并非所有人都需要追求充满野心和冒险的计划，有些人可能更适合安静的小城镇生活。他提出，找到适合自己的社群可以是个性化且多样的，不一定要追随主流的成功路径。（例子：neilv对自己理想城镇的描述）

• 有些人则强调了身份认同和失败对个人发展的影响。Lucasfcosta指出，很多人过于执着于某个失败的身份标签，而不是客观看待失败本身。他认为，转变心态，接受失败只是特定时间的经历，而非个人永久属性，是重要的。（例子：lucasfcosta对失败的看法）

• 关于对拒绝的免疫力，Nathan_compton批评了一些创始人因对拒绝免疫而导致的破坏性行为，认为这种态度虽然有助于创业，但也可能带来负面影响。他认为，抗拒社会压力是有代价的。（例子：nathan_compton在 startup 中的负面经历）

• 有些人分享了实际建议，鼓励毕业生通过旅行和体验不同的文化找到自己的兴趣和热情。Famahar建议每个毕业生去国外体验工作假期，通过接触不同的生活和职业方式，找到自己真正热爱和讨厌的事物。（例子：famahar的个人推荐）

• 另一个值得注意的观点是，良好的社交网络可以提升个人对自我潜力的期望。Ariztocray分享了自己在遇到更有成就的人之后，如何提高自我期望并实现超越原先预期的成就。（例子：ariztocray的个人经历）

补充讨论：
• 部分评论者对演讲内容的深度和细节提出了进一步的期望，比如jll29希望了解更多关于演讲者如何找到自己职业道路的具体经历和细节。（例子：jll29对更多细节的渴望）

• 还有一些技术社区的讨论，如jackphilson认为文化契合和社群对个人发展至关重要，并引入了网络国家的概念。（例子：jackphilson对网络国家的看法）

• 最后，有些人如vzaliva认为，有些人生经验无法通过建议或教导获得，必须通过个人的试错过程来发现。（例子：vzaliva对演讲内容的反思）

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于毕业后如何面对“无轨”状态以及如何找到适合自己的社群和方向。一方面，有些人认为应尽早意识到“无轨”状态并主动探索，另一方面，有些人认为找到适合自己的安静生活和社群同样重要，不一定要追求主流的成功。

44074017.article_content:
Thank you to Bucknell University for inviting me to be this year's commencement speaker. And congratulations to the Class of 2025!
Watch the speech on YouTube
.
Thirty-two years ago I was sitting where you are now. At least, I assume I was. I can't really remember anything about my own graduation. I was too hung over.
The main thing I remember from that time in my life is that I had no plan. I had a degree in English, no job, and no idea what I even wanted to do. I would have liked to work hard on something I cared about. But I didn't have anything I cared about, and it took me a decade to find one.
Maybe I can help you do that faster. Maybe I can help you figure out what to work on.
You fall into three groups. Some of you already have all kinds of ambitious plans. You're already admitted to med school for the fall, or whatever. Others of you have no ambitious plans and no desire to have any. You just want to have a happy life, and that's cool. But in the middle, there's a group who wish they had ambitious plans, but don't. This speech is for you. I'm going to tell you how to get ambitious plans.
The first step is to realize that the subway stops here. Up to this point in life, most of you have been rolling on train tracks. Elementary school, middle school, high school, college—it was always clear what the next stop was. In the process you've been trained to believe something that’s not true: that
all
of life is train tracks. And there are some jobs where you can make it stay like train tracks if you want, but really today is the last stop.
This fact is so terrifying that a lot of people try to remain in denial about it. (I certainly did.) But it's also exciting. You can go in any direction now.
I didn't realize that, so I looked for more tracks. I looked for a job at a big, well-known company that I hoped would train me to do something, but I didn't know or care what, really, just so long as I was on some new set of tracks. The fall after graduation I was on the night shift at Fidelity Investments customer service, answering people's questions about why the value of their mutual fund went down.
This wasn't fun or interesting to me. So why did I do it? Two reasons: I didn't know any better, and I didn't think I had any particular aptitude for any kind of work, so I was delighted that anyone would pay me to do anything.
So I'm going to tell you about a trick you can pull right here at the point where the train tracks end. You can reinvent yourself. I wish I’d known I could do that. I was lazy in college and got bad grades. But the real problem was that I believed them: I believed that mediocre grades meant I was a mediocre person. And that stuck with me for years. I'm sure most of you have done better in school than I did, but maybe there are some of you who are feeling a little unsure of yourself. But here's the thing: you don't have to tell people that.
They
don't know. So if you want to, you can just decide to shift gears at this point, and no one's going to tell you you can't. You can just decide to be more curious, or more responsible, or more energetic, and no one's going to go look up your college grades and say, "Hey, wait a minute, this person's supposed to be a slacker."
If I'd known then what I know now, I'd have realized that there are many different kinds of jobs you can get after college, some much more interesting than others. And if I'd known I could be more ambitious, I would have tried to get one of the more interesting ones.
The truth is there are thousands of different places you could go work, and you have to consider them all and figure out which is the best. But that sounds impossible, right? You only had to choose between 60 different majors, and now you have to choose between thousands of different jobs? How do you even do that? The first step, is to acknowledge that you have to. You can't just drift into the open mouth of Fidelity, like I did.
Ok, then what? How do you search through thousands of options? To be honest, you can’t. You have to use some kind of trick for narrowing them down. My favorite trick is people. Talk to people. Get introduced to new people. Find the people that you think are interesting, and then ask what they're working on. And if you find yourself working at a place where you don't like the people, get out.
That was how I finally figured out what to work on. I found the
startup people
, and I realized that startups were what I was interested in. Once I did, I got more ambitious. I decided to write a book about startups. And having my own project made me even more ambitious. Finally I was working on something of my own! But most people I told about this project didn't get it. I wasn't an author or a startup person. How could I be writing a book about startups?
Which leads me to my final point about getting ambitious plans: you have to be immune to rejection. People are going to dismiss you at first. If that's enough to stop you, you're doomed. So you have to l

data.title: Postgres IDE in VS Code
data.author: Dowwie
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VS Code中Postgres数据库管理工具的发布及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• **支持VS Code数据库工具的发布**：
   - [jenny91] 对MIT许可证发布表示欢迎。
   - [wolframhempel] 认为VS Code的新工具能减少与PG Admin切换的摩擦，提升开发体验。
   - [saqadri] 表示此工具很酷，并提到Prisma Studio类似的功能，认为VS Code的支持很不错。

• **VS Code与数据库感知编辑器的比较**：
   - [seveibar] 提出VS Code数据库工具与数据库感知编辑器的比较，认为生成的代码/工件少能使代码库更整洁，但也指出并非所有人都使用VS Code或知道如何使用其集成。
   - [bdcravens] 提到VS Code在多显示器工作环境中的不足，偏好使用DataGrip在不同显示器上工作。

• **对不同数据库工具的偏好**：
   - [qntmfred] 表示从SQL Server和SSMS转向Postgres及其工具（如pgAdmin、DBeaver、DataGrip）的不满，认为Postgres的工具生态系统缺乏关注。
   - [FajitaNachos] 习惯使用Postico与Postgres交互，好奇其他Postico用户的使用体验。
   - [nico] 提到VS Code中数据库管理工具的尴尬使用体验，偏好phpMyAdmin或Adminer类的工具。

• **JetBrains与VS Code的对比**：
   - [impalallama] 认为JetBrains的内置数据库工具比VS Code更好。
   - [pwhalen] 认为VS Code新工具目前功能上尚无超越DataGrip，但欢迎竞争者进入这一领域，特别是在AI辅助方面推动JetBrains。

• **AI辅助在数据库管理中的应用**：
   - [weitendorf] 提到AI（如Claude）在Postgres/SQL方面的理解和能力较差，无法信任其在数据库相关的复杂任务上的表现，并好奇其他人是否遇到类似问题。

补充讨论：
• **对VS Code市场定位的讨论**：
   - [Toritori12] 讨论VS Code从“初学者IDE”到最常用IDE的成长，并提到Visual Studio在某些领域的“遗留”状态。

• **工具需求与市场反应**：
   - [pier25] 惊讶此工具为Postgres而非SQL Server发布，暗示Postgres的需求更高。
   - [zamacho] 询问是否有类似的MySQL扩展。

争议焦点：
• **VS Code数据库工具与专用工具（如DataGrip、Postico）的功能和使用体验对比**是讨论中的一个争议点，不同用户对工具的偏好和使用场景各异。

• **AI在数据库管理中的应用问题**，特别是AI对Postgres/SQL的理解和可靠性，是另一个争议点。

data.article_summary: 本文探讨了大型推理模型中中间标记（常被认为是“思维”或推理痕迹）的实际作用，挑战了它们对模型性能有直接影响的假设。作者通过训练transformer模型，对比了在正确和噪声、损坏的推理痕迹数据上的表现，发现即使使用无关或错误的痕迹数据，模型在解决问题时的表现依然与使用正确数据时相似，甚至在某些情况下更优。这表明中间标记的准确性与最终解决方案的正确性之间关系不大，提醒不应过度解读这些痕迹为类似人类或算法行为的证据。

主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLM）的“不合理有效性”现象及其在推理任务中的表现和机制。

不同观点：

• 争议的焦点在于语言模型在推理任务中的表现机制，特别是 CoT（Chain of Thought）是否必要，以及 tokens 的实际意义。
• 讨论还涉及到模型内部计算过程的重要性，以及如何通过自适应计算等方法来优化模型性能。

Title:
Beyond Semantics: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens
Authors:
Kaya Stechly
,
Karthik Valmeekam
,
Atharva Gundawar
,
Vardhan Palod
,
Subbarao Kambhampati
View a PDF of the paper titled Beyond Semantics: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Reasonless Intermediate Tokens, by Kaya Stechly and 4 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Recent impressive results from large reasoning models have been interpreted as a triumph of Chain of Thought (CoT), and especially of the process of training on CoTs sampled from base LLMs in order to help find new reasoning patterns. In this paper, we critically examine that interpretation by investigating how the semantics of intermediate tokens-often anthropomorphized as "thoughts" or reasoning traces and which are claimed to display behaviors like backtracking, self-verification etc.-actually influence model performance. We train transformer models on formally verifiable reasoning traces and solutions, constraining both intermediate steps and final outputs to align with those of a formal solver (in our case, A* search). By constructing a formal interpreter of the semantics of our problems and intended algorithm, we systematically evaluate not only solution accuracy but also the correctness of intermediate traces, thus allowing us to evaluate whether the latter causally influences the former. We notice that, despite significant improvements on the solution-only baseline, models trained on entirely correct traces still produce invalid reasoning traces when arriving at correct solutions. To further show that trace accuracy is only loosely connected to solution accuracy, we then train models on noisy, corrupted traces which have no relation to the specific problem each is paired with, and find that not only does performance remain largely consistent with models trained on correct data, but in some cases can improve upon it and generalize more robustly on out-of-distribution tasks. These results challenge the assumption that intermediate tokens or "Chains of Thought" induce predictable reasoning behaviors and caution against anthropomorphizing such outputs or over-interpreting them (despite their mostly correct forms) as evidence of human-like or algorithmic behaviors in language models.
